Assessment: Ms. X is a 43 yo F with HPV-related squamous cell carcinoma of the vulva/cervix/anus currently treated per 18-C-0056 with M7824 but off treatment since 12/19 due to various complications including psoriatic arthritis.  In 7/20 scans showed systemic progression, with multiple FDG-avid lymph nodes, in addition to progression of local disease in the perianal region. Standard of care systemic therapy could for relapsed/progressive disease would be carbo/paclitaxel; however she has a low burden of disease and it appears to be slow-growing.  On recent mutational testing here, she is MSI stable, so pembrolizumab would not be a standard of care option.  In addition any clinical trial incorporating immune checkpoint inhibitors is somewhat problematic given her psoriatic arthritis, but she is eligible for trial here of triple therapy with IC inhibitor, nHS-12, and vaccine.  Another option avoiding this risk is our HPV vaccine trial here, and this is also acceptable given the slow growth of her day and may be preferable at this time.  She returns to clinic today prior to planned enrollment on protocol 20-C-0045 and she was consented in clinic with Dr. Abdul Sater. We will begin treatment today as planned. Would likely benefit from ongoing GYN involvement given ongoing local disease and we can offer f/u here vs return to local providers per pt preference. Opioids refilled today.

Thyroid Dysfunction - TSH between 4 and 5  - Continue  Levothyroxine 75 mcg PO daily. - CTM TSH/T4

She has mild bleeding from the perianal areas daily and more when she has a BM.

Assessment: Mrs. X is a 43 yo F with recurrent cervical/vulvar SCC and anogenital SCC who presents today for evaluation for prior to week 21 of M7824 for HPV-associated malignancies. Restaging scans 12/17/2019 show stable disease.  - Week 15 and week 17 doses were skipped due to asthma exacerbation - Per Dr. Park outside anal condyloma biopsies is consistent with HSIL and also areas of moderately differentiated SCC. This is not considered to be a new area of cancer. - Her quality of life is affected by symptoms of anal pain and palliative approaches should be considered including but not limited to surgical debulking.  - We also discussed that while M7824 can be decreasing the amount of tumor burden, it could be worsening the precancerous lesions (condyloma, HSIL). In line with that and in light of likely surgery and potential delayed wound healing we would be inclined to hold the treatment today. - She might need to go off the protocol if she does not derive further clinical benefit with M7824 and proceed with chemotherapy vs other trials (potentially combinations with M7824 aimed towards increasing its' efficacy) - Stable gum bleeding and epistaxis have nearly resolved since holding last treatment.  Plan - Will hold week 21 of M7824 - She will remain on Advair and we also prescribed a week of prednisone 40 mg in case she experiences any additional worsening of her asthma - She will notify us if she develops any respiratory symptoms/worsening after today's treatment - Follow up with Dr. Park in regards to plan for anal condyloma debulking - Next restaging in 4 weeks   Staffed with Dr. Strauss

column2: Attending Note:    Ms X is a 43yo F with recurrent, locally advanced vulvar and anal squamous cell cancer, likely HPV related, who comes to clinic to discuss starting trial with M7824. Briefly, at 22yo she was found to have VIN s/p multiple laser resections. In 2007, developed vulvar SCC s/p several resections with eventual TAH (ovaries retained). In 2015, developed recurrent vulvar/Bartholin’s gland SCC s/p incomplete resection to spare vagina and colon, ILNDx, 5FU/Mitomycin/RT (Nigro protocol). In 2019 developed new peri-anal lesion. Path confirmed SCC with positive margins. MRI in July 2019 showed new left vaginal cuff lesion (2.2cm) and path confirmed SCC. PET/CT showed no evidence of distant disease recurrence. She has recurrent, locally advanced vulvar and anal SCC that is not amenable to local resection per gynecology.     At baseline she is known to have guttate psoriasis, bilateral hand arthralgias (no prior use of prednisone/DMARs), intermittent vaginal bleeding and diarrhea dating back to her prior RT therapy. She was seen by dermatology for her psoriasis for baseline assessment. No need for systemic therapy. Bilateral hand arthralgias with negative arthritis serologies (7/31/19). Rheumatology consulted for baseline assessment. Intermittent vaginal bleeding per patient following intercourse. Of note, prior gyn notes report some degree of vaginal bleeding from this vaginal cuff mass. Denies regular or daily bleeding. Denies prior need for blood transfusions. Reports daily liquid/soft stools 2-3x per day. No blood or tarry stools. No h/o hemorrhoids but has h/o radiation proctitis that has resulted in the softer stools.     Labs reviewed. ECOG 1. Measurable disease – 2.2cm vaginal cuff lesion. Reviewed medications – recommended that she stop turmeric due to potential interactions with M7824 and taper of estrogen 2mg given h/o clot risk in the cancer setting.     Had an extensive discussion with pt about mucosal bleeding risk given report of intermittent vaginal bleeding from vaginal cuff lesion. Also discussed that given her guttate psoriasis and possible seronegative arthritis, that these may worsen on treatment. She has never required steroids and is not currently on steroids. We also discussed that given her h/o radiation proctitis, she may develop worsening of her diarrhea and/or blood in her stool. She denies any h/o of blood stools or hemorrhoidal bleeding. Also discussed that give her h/o Xs Palsy in 1997 (no recurrence, no known viral etiology, resolved without intervention), she may have a recurrence given the potential for mononeuropathies seen with ICB. She and her husband acknowledged these risks and wished to proceed with signing the consent form.     Given h/o psoriasis, Dr Strauss d/w medical monitor – okay to proceed. Stop tumeric. Taper estradiol.  Rheumatology consult today for baseline evaluation. Dermatology consulted yesterday. Proceed to treatment today with M7824. RTC 2 weeks per protocol.

column2: Called to oncology clinic to evaluate a skin eruption. Patient started M7824 11/5/19 and developed rash on bilateral cheeks in January and two weeks ago she noticed inflamed small papules on the arms and armpits. The patient think getting hot makes the rash worse, no UV reaction. Patient does not have significant itch. No eye symptoms, no oral complaints. She also has asymptomatic hypothyroidism and recently started levothyroxine. On exam the patient had Fitzpatrick type 4 skin and dark hair. On the malar cheeks are confluent erythematous thin plaques with irregular boarders. Oh the lateral upper arms are minute folliculocentric red papules with slight keratotic spines. Similar keratotic papules are scattered on the upper back and anterior thighs. In the bilateral axilla are clusters of inflammatory papules sparing the vault. This patient has an inflammatory dermatitis that is likely treatment related. Plan to manage symptomatically with topical steroids (HC to face, TAC to body). The eruption on the arms resembles keratosis pilaris. Considering the malar distribution on the face, will consider testing ANA.

Agree with assessment and plan of Dr Simard. Briefly Ms X comes to clinic for week 15 of M7824. Scans 2 weeks ago showed continued PR but tumor markers continue to trend up. On exam today, Ms X reports onset of rash on arms/back/face 2-3 days after her most recent infusion. Denies any new skin lotions, soaps, exposures, etc. Reports some associated pruritis but not interfering with ADLs. Rash on face is bothersome and is worsened by heat/exercise. Labs reviewed - stable. TSH still rising. Ms X did not pick up her synthryoid after the last visit. Strongly encouraged to pick up rx today and start asap to avoid any potential side effects. Ms X was agreeable to start her synthryoid today. Dermatology consulted. Will hold treatment today due to likely inflammatory dermatitis.  Will start topical steroids per Dr Brownell and reassess in 2 weeks.  As above, rising tumor markers noted. Restaging in 4 weeks.

Assessment: 35F Spanish-speaking with metastatic HPV 16 associated metastatic cervical SCC s/p 6 cycles cisplatin/paclitaxel with minimal measurable disease now on NHS-IL-12.    Scans 10/15/19 show stable disease with target lesion, left common iliac lymph node stable at 2.1 cm x 1.5 cm, compared to baseline (2.4x1.7cm), and with no new lesions.  The patient denies any complaints and is doing well overall.  However, her CA 19-9, which was significantly elevated at the start of treatment (near 4000) has risen over the last few weeks and is up to 183 at last visit (todays result of 406 came after the patient was seen in clinic).  This is concerning for recurrence of disease (possibly peritoneal carcinomatosis) not yet picked up on imaging.  These findings were discussed in detail with the patient and daughter (with interpreter present) and options were presented to continue with treatment today and to monitor the rise of this marker versus switching to the M7824 (HPV-trap) trial.  For now, the patient, who feels well, decided to continued with the current IL-12 treatment and we will continue to monitor the CA 19-9.   We will proceed with IL-12 treatment today.

Since he had good response from prior cisplatin and paclitaxel, repeating same chemotherapy is an option, although poor response rates in the third line setting and he is reluctant to proceed with chemotherapy due to side effects.   We are screening him for one of our clinical trials. Since he didn’t have previous radiation therapy, he will not be qualified for our birinapant re-irradiation trial. However, he is appears to be an appropriate candidate for our Phase II Trial of M7824 in Subjects with HPV Associated Malignancies. Early data from a small cohort of patients with HPV associated malignancies in a phase I trial of M7824 has shown promising activity (NCT02517398).  His major problems include an abnormal creatinine >1.5 (but with CrCl>50), and history of hearing problems (patient denies symptoms). Both problems could be explained by platinum use. He is scheduled for an official audiology exam. In addition his viral studies remain pending and hence his enrollment.
He was counselled on all options potentially available, autonomy, risk and benefit of drugs offered on Protocol #18C0056.
He voiced understanding and anticipates to start next Tuesday if his labs come back negative.
We advised with IV hydration every time he gets his scans done.
Audiology eval in the interim for hearing loss.

Presents for C2D1 18-c-0056 M7824.  Today, Mr. Xs continues to endorse fatigue and RUQ pain. The fatigue is worse compared to 2 weeks ago. He did have 3 days period where energy level was much improved but now worse again since last week. Also notes headaches for last 2 weeks. Denies associated neurological symptoms including double vision or focal weakness. Using Tylenol with some relief. Last head imaging was >1 year ago. Does not tolerate MRI due to clostophobia. Peripheral neuropathy persists bilaterally in hands and feet. Did not trial Neurontin yet. For pain control, continues to Vape and used Oxycodone * 3 doses at night, with some improvement. ALso notes mild nausea over last 2 weeks with one episode of emesis on 10.29. Otherwise no other new symptoms.  Denies fevers, chills, CP. Exertional SOB persists.

In 3/2017, Mr. X presented with rectal bleeding. A biopsy that was taken during colonoscopy on 3/15/17 and showed in situ, non-keratinizing SCC with foci suspicious for invasion. A repeat biopsy on 4/13/17 revealed basaloid SCC, p16 positive. MR showed a T4 anorectal tumor invading prostate, seminal vesicle, base of penis, and encasing membranous urethra as well as R inguinal LN metatastases. He was staged cT4N2M0

On 4/15/17 he was taken to the OR for a laparoscopic colostomy in preparation for treatment (reversed in 1/2018). Another bx of the anal tumor was done and showed invasive SCC, mod differentiated; p16 IHC stain diffusely positive.

Between 5/3/17 - 7/11/17 he underwent CXRT with mitomycin and xeloda, receiving a total of 4698 cGy in 29fx to the anus and LNs. His treatment was interrupted half-way 2/2 iliitis and C.diff. Follow-up colonoscopy on 8/9/17 and MRI on 8/26/17 showed NED.

Surveillance PET in 11/2017 revealed fdg avid liver lesion which an MRI in 12/2018 confirmed. On 1/2/18 he went for a planned ablation which was aborted when the lesion was found to have doubled in size from 1.4 to 3cm. 7/2018: Patient reports that her symptoms started with left lower leg swelling and then she started having heavy vaginal bleeding. Her last pap smear was in 2010 and reportedly was normal.

10/2018: She subsequently was seen by her PCP for the left leg swelling and was diagnosed with a LLE DVT. She was on Pradaxa, then Xarelto then switched to Eliquis anticoagulation due to medical insurance coverage issues.

11/2/16: She presented to Saint Agnes Hospital ER for severe left leg pain and swelling now moving into her left lower back and abdomen. The pain and swelling was so severe she was unable to walk. She was found to have AKI (creatinine 5.0) and bilateral hydronephrosis. Imaging revealed a large pelvic mass(3cm x3cm) as well as a large left pelvic sidewall mass(12x7x16cm). She was admitted and on 11/5/18 and 11/7/18 she had right and then left percutaneous nephrostomies placed. On 11/9/18 she underwent a pelvic exam under anesthesia and had a cervical biopsy which revealed invasive moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma with background necrosis(see path below). She also underwent an IR aspiration of her pelvic sidewall cystic mass. Her back pain improved temporarily. On 11 /14/18 she was discharged home with oncology follow-up.
CERVIX, BIOPSY 11/12/18: INVASIVE SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA, MODERATELY DIFFERENTIATED.
Pelvic Fluid, Left (18CY-514, 11109/18): POSITIVE FOR MALIGNANT CELLS. Squamous cell carcinoma.

11 /28/18: She re-presented to the UMMC ER for left low back pain radiating down her leg and to establish care. She was admitted to the gynecologic oncology service. PET/CT showed the following: There is a large metabolically active necrotic cervical mass, consistent with the primary malignancy. Large, metabolically active hypoattenuating multiloculated collection involving the left psoas and iliacus muscles with central photopenia and associated erosive changes of the left acetabulum and femoral head, is most consistent with necrotic muscular metastasis. Metabolically active right hilar, retroperitoneal and iliac lymphadenopathy is consistent with additional metastasis.
12/17/18: Started external beam pelvic radiation therapy.
12/24/18: Started cycle #1 cisplatin chemotherapy. Cycle #2 12/31/18. Cycle #3 1/7/19.
12/27/19: She was seen in the UMMC ER because she ran out of pain meds. She had a Candida albicans and Serratia UTI treated with Diflucan and Bactrim.
1/9/19: Completed external beam pelvic radiation therapy(total of 15 fractions).

2/13/19: Follow-up FDG PET/CT showed resolution of FDG avidity and decrease in size of the cervical mass, and the large multiloculated fluid collection in the left pelvis. Interval resolution of right hilar and multiple FDG avid retroperitoneal as well as bilateral iliac lymph nodes. There is a residual non-FDG avid lymph node in the internal iliac chain. Constellation of these findings are suggestive of favorable response to treatment. There is a small hypoattenuating lesion in the hepatic segment VI with mild FDG uptake which may represent early metastasis and should be followed up with further imaging.

64 YOF with metastatic HPV+ cervical squamous cell carcinoma. Treatment history includes: carboplatin/paclitaxel/bev, single-agent bevacizumab, single-agent pemetrexed, and carboplatin/gemcitabine. She is currently enrolled under protocol 18-c-0056 and received W1 of M7824 on 4/8/2020. She has received 1 dose of M7824 to date.

Interval History: A few days after the last televisit, Ms Galloway developed abdominal bloating and some right sided back pain. She was diagnosed with a UTI and was treated with Bactrim. The abdominal bloating did not improve. Due to concerns for PD, I asked her to follow-up with her primary oncologist for a clinical assessment. Since that time, she underwent a paracentesis with removal of 1.5L of ascitic fluid. She also had a PET last week which is suggestive of progressive disease.
Primary Oncologist: Christine Lee, Texas Oncology (Woodlands, Houston)
History of HPV since 1990s, treated with Cryosurgery ~1990, followed with pap smears until 2014
Winter 2014: Pap smear showing evidence of adenocarcinoma. Followed up with cone biopsy
7/2/2014: FIGO Stage IB1 adenocarcinoma of the endocervix. Treated with radical hysterectomy, BSO, PLND, by Dr. Geri Fromm. Pelvic lymph nodes were negative for metastases
5/2018: Recurrence in the abdomen (symptoms of abdominal distension, RUQ tenderness), with peritoneal carcinomatosis, omental biopsy lap confirms metastatic mucin secreting adenocarcinoma.
6/13/2018 – 9/27/2018: Initiation of carboplatin and paclitaxel x6 cycles. Bevacizumab added to cycle #2.
8/10/2018: Interval PET/CT after 3 cycles shows no significant metabolic activity, resolution of metabolic
activity in the hilar regions, improvement in ascites, and significant improvement in the peritoneal implants with a near-complete response.
3/21/2019: PET/CT scan is negative for metastases
6/20/2019: PET/CT scan is negative for metastases

9/12/2019: CT scan reveals interval development of omental caking and malignant abdominal ascites. A soft tissue mass is present in the left anterior pelvis measuring 2 cm in size and demonstrating an SUV of 84.
11/21/2019 PET/CT demonstrates progression in the left lower pelvis, and relatively stable disease
12/10/2019 – 1/21/2020:  Carboplatin + gemcitabine x 3 cycles, stopped for progression (new lesion behind bladder)
12/27/2019: CARIS testing on the omentum reveals MSI stable, mismatch repair status proficient, PDL1-, high risk HPV positive, tumor mutational burden intermediate.
3/11/2020: Enrolled on 11-C-0225 and received D1 of NHSIl12
4/7/2020: Early restaging due to rapidly rising tumor markers on NHSIL12 showed PD. Changed to M7824 with Week 1 on 4/8/2020.
Today Ms Galloway and I spoke on Microsoft Teams.  We discussed that since her first dose of M7824, she has noticed a few new symptoms.

#Hematuria - Starting around 1-2 days after her treatment, she noticed some scant blood on the tissue in the morning when she blows her nose. No blots, no need for packing. Only occurs first thing in the morning. It occurred daily from a few days after treatment until a few days ago. She also reports intermittent pink urine (hematuria) that occurred in the first few days after the treatment. No clots and this is consistent with the hematuria she normally experiences after exercise but she reports avoiding exercise in the last 2 weeks. No clots or frank blood, just pink tinged urine that has self-resolved. No associated dysuria, increased frequency, or urgency.

# Skin rash - She also reports a new rash on her chest, back and arms that started a few days ago as well as 2 episodes of lip swelling (3 days ago was the lower lip, 2 days ago it was the upper lip, none last night). She does report a new detergent (due to difficulty getting her normal detergent during COVID shortages) and has washed cloth face masks in this detergent. Lip swelling and rash has improved with benadryl. We discussed that while always possible that it is due to M7824, it is more likely due to the detergent due to the delayed onset.

# Abdominal bloating - She reports that prior to receiving her first dose of M7824, she had some abdominal pain that resolved in the days after her first dose. However, shortly after that she noticed she started feeling bloated. No recent change in diet. She is having regular bowel movements with no recent change in bowel calibur or consistency. In addition, she is passing gas regularly. No blood in the stool and no obvious motility issues. She also reports no issues with eating and denies early satiety.

# Anxiety - She continued to have significant anxiety about traveling to NCI due to the risk of COVID. This is compounded by her anxiety about delaying treatment with M7824. We talked extensively about this today.
# Fevers/Mylagias - started on Sunday (3 days ago) and persistent into Monday. However, she felt fine yesterday and today. She was tested for COVID earlier this week and is awaiting the results.
Aside from the above symptoms, she continues good energy and works full time (although is on quarantine currently due to the fever earlier this week). Appetite is good as above.

Assessment: 64yoF with metastatic HPV+ cervical adenocarcinoma s/p multiple lines of treatment including NHS-IL12, now on M7824. This is week 5.   Due to her concerns about COVID, Ms Galloway opted for a televisit rather than an inpatient visit. She had labs performed locally and results were sent to the research team for review. She also had a PET scan done on 4/30/20 with her oncologist.   PET showed multiple, bilateral lung nodules with largest at 1.2cm in LLL. Review of last CT showed a LLL nodule around 9mm. Also mention of multiple hypemetabolic liver lesions, however, size and number not specified. Also noted to have enlargement of peritoneal implants but size of measurements not specifically mentioned. Omental disease also seemed to have progressed and pt now with pocketed ascites. Only occurs first thing in the morning. It occurred daily from a few days after treatment until a few days ago. She also reports intermittent pink urine (hematuria) that occurred in the first few days after the treatment. No clots and this is consistent with the hematuria she normally experiences after exercise but she reports avoiding exercise in the last 2 weeks. column2: Agree with assessment and plan of Dr Jenkins. Briefly Ms Galloway comes to clinic for D29 of NHSIL12. Restaging was done early due to increasing tumor markers and patient concerns she was progressing. Scans today do show enlargement of target lesions as well as 2 new lesions in her liver. This is consistent with progressive disease and she will come off treatment with NHSIL12. It has been 4 weeks since her first dose so per protocol she has completed her DLT period. No DLTs. ECOG 0.   Labs reviewed today - low grade AST/ALT elevation has resolved. Initial UA with 3+ proteinuria but also with multiple squamous cells suggestive of a dirty UA. Repeat UA without proteinuria and much improved overall. Otherwise labs at goal. Symptomatically, she has no residual side effects from treatment with NHSIL12.    Today we discussed the risks and benefits of starting M7824. We discussed potential immune-related toxicities as well as the potential for mucosal bleeding. She has baseline intermittent hematuria that started after she had her ureteral stent placed in June 2018. She reports she notices pink urine after she works out or if she is dehydrated. She reports that yesterday she exercised for 45 minutes and also feels that she is dehydrated. She didnt drink much fluid on the plane to DC and didnt drink this morning due to the CT scan. Her repeat UA was after she drank water and the protein and hematuria has mostly cleared. I discussed that she is at risk for mucosal bleeding from M7824. Currently she denies blood clots in her urine and again, reports only intermittent pink urine that is tired to exercise or dehydration. I encouraged her to stay hydrated while on trial. She is eager to start treatment and will be consented tomorrow morning (4/8) with plans to start treatment immediately following.

Treatment Summary: 80 yo M with Stage IVa p16+ pT2N2b squamous cell carcinoma of the left tonsil (dx 1/2017, PD-L1 TOPS 25%) metastatic to bone, liver, and periportal & periceliac/peripancreatic LN s/p left neck dissection, transoral robotic surgery with left radical tonsil and base of tongue resection, radiation, excision of soft tissue mass in sternal area, carboplatin/paclitaxel x5, nivolumab, and phase II trial of monalizumab and cetuximab.    Of note, has also been treated for pulmonary MAC (started 6/26/2019).   The patient was enrolled in clinical trial 18-c-0056 and had been treated with M7824 (PD-L1/TGF-beta trap), Week 1 was 6/25/2019. He received 3 treatments in total (second being on 7/23/19 and last being 9/3/2019). Treatment course was complicated by psoriasis flares and bleeding (due to M7824 plus VWD plus Prophylactic dose of LMWH (lowered from treatment dose for his Afib)) and IDA for which he received blood and iron transfusions. We diagnosed him with Heydes syndrome (Ao Stenosis and vwF disease), resolved s/p TAVR, and bleeding stopped. Currently on rivaroxaban. He had a mixed response with the periportal lesion growing and treated with palliative radiation. After radiation, his liver (abscopal) and periportal lesions shrank down.

Interim History/Review of Systems: Interval Updates/Subjective:  He was last seen in this clinic on 6/1/21. Since that time a PET showed progression of sternal metastasis, a T4 mass, and new hepatic mets. An MRI of the thoracic spine showed that the T4 vertebral mass was invading the epidural space. The patient remained asymptomatic. He proceeded with 2 fractions of radiation to the T4 mass on 6/21/21. He recently completed his post-treatment dexamethasone.   Today he presents to clinic for screening for protocol 20-C-0045.  He is feeling generally well. We discussed the following:  - Continues to have trouble swallowing. Manages well with chewable tablets where able - Orthostatic hypotension which is manageable with behavioral modifications - Continues to use a cane for walking. He notes instability. No weakness. No falls. - Intermittent loss of focus in R eye for which he has seen Ophto - Has a ""curtain"" cross his vision intermittently. Has occurred with both eyes. Happens for a few seconds approximately once every 5-6 months. Most recently occurred last month. No associated neurologic symptoms except on one occasion when he felt too disoriented to rise from his seat. - Occasional sweats at night but not drenching night sweats.   He denies neck or back pain. No new symptoms.
Transoral robotic surgery with left radical tonsil and base of tongue resection
Excision of soft tissue mass in sternal area
Infection History: negative 6/21 prior MAC - s/p treatment (completed)

Oncology History: Oncologic History: 9/2016 - Developed left neck mass. He was treated with antibiotics without relief.  11/2016 - Per the patient, he underwent bronchoscopy, which showed that he had cancer. 1/16/17 – Pathologic staging was Stage IV A (T2, N2b, M0) 1/30/17 – Underwent left neck dissection.  2/7/17 - Underwent TORS (transoral robotic surgery) resection of left radical tonsil and base of tongue. Pathology of left radical tonsil and base of tongue showed squamous cell carcinoma, poorly differentiated, 3.1 cm. Margins negative for tumour. This was consistent with T2N2b disease, resected with negative margins. There were two positive LNs, neither with extracapsular extension. Unclear how many LNs sampled. Pathology from sternal area soft tissue showed metastatic squamous cell carcinoma. Immunostains for CK5/6, p40, and p16 are positive, and compatible with metastasis from patient’s known head and neck primary.  5/10/17 – Received radiation ending on 5/10/17.  9/18/17 – PET showed no disease in the head and neck, but there was interval increased avidity of previously seen osseous lesions and multiple new FDG avid lesions c/w progression of disease.  10/2/17 – Underwent excision of soft tissue mass in sternal area. column2: 9/2016 - Developed left neck mass. He was treated with antibiotics without relief.

5/10/19 – CT chest showed developing 2.9x2.4x2.8 cm mass in the RLL of lung. A 5 mm pleural-based RML nodule is unchanged. CT A/P showed hepatic metastases and increasing periportal lymphadenopathy. CT head showed no evidence of metastatic disease.

5/23/19 – CT neck showed left tonsillectomy, hemiglossectony, and partial oropharyngectomy. No definite evidence of local recurrence. Left neck dissection. No pathologic cervical LNs by imaging criteria. Other grossly unchanged lung nodules. Mildly prominent mediastinal and hilar LNs, stable to minimally increased in size, nonspecific in etiology. Stable sclerotic osseous metastases. CT A/P showed large periceliac/peripancreatic node (2.9x3.0 cm), increased since 12/18/18, suspicious for a metastatic node. Multiple small poorly defined hypoenhancing areas in the liver, not seen on prior PET/CTs, suspicious for hepatic metastases. There is a 5 mm sclerotic area in the L2 vertebral body that is indeterminate, but similar to 12/18/18. Prostate is enlarged with asymmetric enhancement in the right gland although this is nonspecific on CT.

6/3/19 – CT-FNA of RLL of lung showed necrotizing granulomas involving lung parenchyma, no tumour seen. Infectious etiology (mycobacterial or fungal) is favoured. No acid fast or fungal organisms seen on AFB and Grocott stains performed. Pathology showed blood and scattered epithelioid cells, favour histiocytes/mesothelial cells.

Other grossly unchanged lung nodules. Mildly prominent mediastinal and hilar LNs, stable to minimally increased in size, nonspecific in etiology. Stable sclerotic osseous metastases. CT A/P showed large periceliac/peripancreatic node (2.9x3.0 cm), increased since 12/18/18, suspicious for a metastatic node. Multiple small poorly defined hypoenhancing areas in the liver, not seen on prior PET/CTs, suspicious for hepatic metastases. There is a 5 mm sclerotic area in the L2 vertebral body that is indeterminate, but similar to 12/18/18. Prostate is enlarged with asymmetric enhancement in the right gland although this is nonspecific on CT.

6/3/19 – CT-FNA of RLL of lung showed necrotizing granulomas involving lung parenchyma, no tumour seen. Infectious etiology (mycobacterial or fungal) is favoured. No acid fast or fungal organisms seen on AFB and Grocott stains performed. Pathology showed blood and scattered epithelioid cells, favour histiocytes/mesothelial cells.

column2: Called to see patient in oncology clinic to evaluate pruritic rash on left arm. Patient has had complaint of itching eruption on left arm for multiple weeks. She has been off M7824 since February. Patient has dry skin and uses moisturizer but stopped moisturizing the left arm when the rash started. She has treated the area with OTC hydrocortisone, colloidal silver, tea tree oil, and most recently nystatin. Thy nystatin has improved the itch. Patient is a 38 year old Female. Current Attending is Strauss.
Ms. X is a 38 y/o female w/ metastatic cervical SCC who returns for week 3 treatment on protocol 18-c-0056, M7824 in HPV associated Malignancies.
Here today for C3 of treatment with the M7824.

Ms. X was in her usual state of good health until 2012 when she first sought medical attention for abnormal menstrual bleeding, post-coital bleeding, and spotting. She finally underwent LEEP on 1/25/13, where pathology confirmed showed invasive SCC; a PET scan around that time was negative for metastatic disease.

On 3/20/13 she underwent radical trachelectomy w/ pelvic LND; Pathology showed invasive SCC w/ extensive angiolymphatic invasion. 2/15 pelvic LNs were found to be involved. Margins were negative but free-floating fragments of carcinoma were found in the parametria.

The decision was made that she should undergo completion hysterectomy. This was done on 4/23/13 together w/ L oophorectomy and R oophoropexy. Path showed no residual carcinoma. She was staged TNM stage pT1b1 pN1, FIGO Stage IIIB
She went on to have adjuvant CXRT w/weekly cisplatin; 50Gy to pelvis, 45Gy to para-aortic nodes, which completed on 7/10/13: Post-treatment PET in 9/2013 revealed NED.

Two years later, in 9/2015 she was found to have developed a  port-site recurrence in L abdominal wall, located in L internal/external oblique/ transverse abdominis; CT-guided FNA on 9/25/18 showed metastatic keratinizing SCC c/w cervical SCC.
On 10/22/15 she underwent WLE of anterior abdominal wall and intraoperative RT. Follow-up PET 2/2016 again showed NED.

Two years later, in 1/2018, a surveillance PET scan revealed suspicious L supraclavicular and superior mediastinal LNs, so on 2/1/18, she had a FNA of a L level IV LN which showed metastatic carcinoma thought to be consistent w/ cervical primary (material was insufficient to perform IHC or HPV testing to further evaluate primary site).
Between 2/24/18 and 5/7/18 she received XRT to the painful L supraclavicular adenopathy to a total of 3000cGy in 10fx. Follow-up PET revealed a partial response.

On 7/6/18 an MRI abdominal wall again showed a soft tissue lesion along inner L rectus abdominis muscle and Bx suprapubic rectus abdominis muscle reveals metastatic SCC, so on 8/16/18: she underwent WLE of L rectus abdominis muscle along with laser ablation of vulva for lymphangiectasia and WLE of skin and L anterior abd wall defect reconstruction.
10/30/18: Received first treatment of M7824 on Protocol 18-c-0056.
Ms. X came back today for C3 of treatment, she reports the following symptoms:

> Pain- patient has a chronic pain to her lower back radiating to left side and LLQ which seems to be better controlled with the current regimen. Last visit the dose of Oxycontin ER was increased to 40mg BID and this is helping.
> LE edema- progressively worsening, no clinical evidence of infection, very likely related to her disease but  we will do a US doppler b/l to r/o DVT today.
> feeling tired with some episode of low grade temperature.
Of note, patient is a very poor historian, which makes difficult to tease down her symptoms. She needs to be constantly redirect while she reports her symptoms.

He completed 6 cycles of carboplatin/5-FU/pembrolizumab with initial response. However, shortly after completion of chemotherapy with continued single-agent pembrolizumab, progression of disease was noted on 09/09/19. last pembro dose was on 8/24/2019.  Patient had Week 1 18-c-0056 on 11/5/19. Hospitalized as above for intralesional bleeding 12/7-12/10. Imaging today shows clear evidence of progression at this time, likely at least partially responsible for his feeling of abdominal fullness. At this time, he will be taken off treatment due to both POD and his bleeding episode.   Moving forward, we discussed that his disease has rapidly progressed and that we are concerned that delay in providing next line cytotoxic chemotherapy could result in his tumor worsening his functional status and preventing treatment in the future. For this reason, we will discuss with his primary oncologist as well as the Phase 1 team to discuss treatment options moving forward.
-- Taken off treatment today as above
-- Will follow-up with phase 1 team and home oncologist re: treatment options moving forward
-- Will prescribe Miralax and magnesium citrate for continued constipation in addition to current regimen

column2: Saw Mr X with MO fellow Dr Pegna, and agree with plan. In light of the possible association of the hepatic intralesional hematoma with the M7824, we will not continue treatment, given that a recurrent similar bleeding episode would be a very significant risk. In addition, disease assessment today reveals findings of progression not only outside, but also outside the liver, which more likely than not represents true disease progression. We would recommend treatment with a modality that would offer more chance for immediate disease control, such as chemotherapy or chemoimmunotherapy or adoptive cellular treatments; to that purpose we will contact his KP primary oncologist as well as our Developmental Therapeutic team and the ACT team.

Assessment: Mr. X is a 62 YOM with metastatic p16-positive squamous cell carcinoma of the base of the L-side of the tongue. He was initially diagnosed in 2014 and was treated with concurrent radiation and cisplatin x 6 cycles with CR. In late 2018, the patient developed abdominal pain in the setting of elevated alk phos and weight loss and was found to have cholecystitis. CT performed at that time incidentally noted metastatic disease to the liver. Pathology confirmed metastatic squamous cell carcinoma, strongly p16 positive, PD-L1 CPS score 21. He completed 6 cycles of carboplatin/5-FU/pembrolizumab with initial response. However, shortly after completion of chemotherapy with continued single-agent pembrolizumab, progression of disease was noted on 09/09/19. He presents to the NIH today for evaluation regarding clinical trial eligibility.   Labs were reviewed and significant for elevated alk phos (259; 640 in Jan 2019) and mildly elevated LFTs (ALT 61, AST 48). Imaging performed today showed progressive disease burden. Enlarging liver mets, portahepatis lymphadenopathy, indeterminate rectosigmoid thickening, and a minimal L1 vertebral body compression fracture were noted. We discussed options for treatment at this time, including enrollment onto protocol 18-c-0056 for treatment with the bifunctional fusion protein that combines a monoclonal antibody for PD-L1 and a soluble extracellular domain of the human TGF-beta receptor II. The former provides immunotherapy, and the latter serves as a “trap” for TGF-beta signaling, which has been noted to be overexpressed in HPV-associated cancers. Risks, benefits, potential side effects, and alternatives were discussed with the patient and his wife and he decided to enroll in protocol 18-c-0056. Will plan for a new biopsy at next visit with subsequent enrollment and initiation of therapy.

Plan: # HPV-associated squamous cell carcinoma of the L base of the tongue with new metastatic disease to the liver and portaheptis lymph nodes. - Will plan on repeat biopsy of disease at next visit with subsequent consent and initiation of treatment under protocol 18-c-0056

Summary: Michael Renard  X  is a 49 yo AA M with recurrent metastatic squamous cell carcinoma (cervical nodal mets and pulmonary mets) initially T2N2 at diagnosis.  He underwent definitive chemoradiation in early 2018 with cis/RT yielding CR.  He recurred with new pulmonary disease and cervical node in 9/2019.  Currently follows at NCI/NIH for treatment with M7824 on protocol 18-C-0056.

11/2017- He initially developed difficulty swallowing with bilateral neck adenopathy, particularly on the right and sensation of food getting stuck in the throat. CT neck 11/18/17 showed extensive bilateral adenopathy and right base of tongue asymmetry. PET showed FOG avid mass centered in the base of tongue with involvement of the floor of mouth and intrinsic tongue musculature, measuring approximately 3.7 x 3.7 cm, bilateral hypermetabolic cervical adenopathy, largest node 3.6 cm. No evidence of distant disease. Biopsy of the left valleculae and a left neck lymph node confirmed poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma. He saw Dr. Judd and surgery was discussed but this was felt that it would be too morbid for him.

1/5/2018-2/22/2018-Concurrent chemoradiation was recommended instead and he completed 3 cycles of cisplatin 100 mg/m2 every 3 weeks from 1/5/2018-2/22/2018 and received radiation therapy at the same time. He required temporary PEG placement to maintain nutrition.
6/28/2018-PET scan post-treatment on 6/28/18 showed no evidence of disease.

9/2019-He was then doing well clinically until 9/2019 when PCP obtained an ultrasound of his thyroid and found a 3.3 cm mass lesion most concerning for recurrent nodal metastatic disease. He then underwent a PET-CT on 10/1 that showed no evidence of disease at R tongue base but was concerning for recurrent metastatic disease in the lungs. He underwent biopsy in 10/19 through Kaiser and we are in the process of obtaining that pathology sample for analysis.
He follows with Dr. Iva Ferreira at Kaiser and last saw her in the clinic in late September. Most recent labs on 10/4/2019 showed BMP 138/4.7/101/27/15/1.62, CBC 4.4, 12.5/37.0/240.

His energy and appetite levels are good and he has not had any fevers, chills, night sweats, easy bruising, fatigability, headaches, weakness, weight change, chest pain, shortness of breath, cough, difficulty swallowing, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, abdominal pain, urinary symptoms, leg swelling, rashes, muscle pains, joint pains, or other concerning symptoms.
11/19/2019 - Week 1 Day 1 of 18-C--0056 with M7824 agent.  Baseline AEs: hypothyroid, intermittent nausea.
12/17/2019 - Week 5 treatment held due to nose bleeds with anemia.  Seen by ENT who recommended nasal spray, ointment, humidifer.
01/14/2020 - Week 9 treatment held due to bleeding and fatigue.
01/28/2020 - Week 11 treatment held due to elevated liver enzymes.  Advised to discontinue alcohol and supplement use.

12 point ROS otherwise unremarkable.
ECOG PS 1.

Assessment: Michael  X  is a 49-year-old African-American male with HPV-related metastatic squamous cell carcinoma (cervical nodal mets and pulmonary mets) initially T2N2 at diagnosis, status post definitive chemoradiation in early 2018 with cisplatin/RT.  Recurrence to lungs and cervical node in 9/2019.  Currently on treatment with M7824 per protocol 18-C-0056 (C1D1 = 11/19/19).  Initial restaging showed PD, but second restaging showed shrinking lesions.  Unconfirmed PD.  Most recent imaging 3/19/2020 shows some growth, pending official RECIST measurements with Dr. Bagheri.  Week 9 treatment was held due to nose bleeds and fatigue.  Fatigue has improved.  Cosyntropin test was negative for adrenal insufficiency.  Patient developed hypothyroidism on study likely secondary to autoimmune side effect of M7824.  He is currently on an appropriate dose of exogenous thyroid replacement at 125 mcg/day.    Week 11 treatment was held due to abnormal liver enzymes.  Unknown etiology - possible contributing factors include alcohol, supplement use, or M7824.  Patient discontinued alcohol and supplement use and treatment was held.  Labs show ongoing elevated liver enzymes (grade 1 elevation) and pancreas enzymes.  Week 13, 15, 17 treatments received.  Today will proceed with Week 19 treatment restarted two weeks prior.  ECOG 1
Metastatic Recurrent HPV related SCC (pulmonary, cervical nodal): On M7824. Initial staging imaging on 11/12/2019
- W19D1 of M7824 under protocol 18-C-0056 (M7824 1200 mg IV infusion given q2weeks)
- Likely secondary to dry weather and M7824.  Seen by ENT.
Elevated SCr: Likely CKD related to prior Cisplatin treatment, however cannot rule out other causes
- Recommend no alcohol or supplement use.
- Fatigue has improved on appropriate dose of thyroid medication.
- Increase Levothyroxine to 150 mcg/day on 3/24/20 due to elevated TSH.
- Discussed possible depression vs organic causes.  Will try to increase exercise and activity.

column2: Saw Mr  X  with MO Fellow Dr DeMaria, and agree with his assessment and plan. Mr  X  is tolerating treatment well; the epistaxis episodes and the liver enzyme elevations that had led (on different occasions) to skipping treatments have returned to minor. His most recent imaging on 3/19 on our preliminary review of the images displays some apparent increase in the size of the lung lesions. In the absence of symptoms and in anticipation of standard RECIST assessment with our designated radiologist, Dr Bagheri, we will treat today, and tentatively schedule for repeat imaging assessment in 4 weeks, rather than the 6 as originally planned. In the interim we will communicate with his KP Oncologist to coordinate plan in case of disease progression. This plan was discussed with Mr  X  by writer in DH.

column2: The patient has been seen with the resident in clinic.  Agree with his assessment and plan with the following addition. The patient has developed while on trial new subcutaneous nodules which were felt to be relatively progressive disease, with an intent to treat despite progression allowing for evaluation of immunotherapy effect, which could be delayed.  The patient has underwent surgical resection and also freezing of several of the subcutaneous nodules.  He was left with few lesions notably on the anterior abdominal wall of about a size of 1 cm or less each.  These lesions were evident on CT scan.  We had a discussion in the previous visit with the patient about the potential of palliatively radiating these lesions to remove them.  We arranged for follow-up with radiation oncology with Dr. Jennifer Jones.  The patients evaluation has looked into the various lesions that Could be potentially radiated.  It was felt that the mediastinal/chest lesions are the lesions of interest should the patient benefit most from a radiation therapy.  After this evaluation, we had a discussion with Dr. Jones and including Dr. Julius Strauss.  The consensus is that to wait for the next restaging in 2 weeks, and if the patient was continuously progressing to decide on palliative reradiating his lung lesions, including the currently considered target lesion on the right side.  This will be done mainly to prevent progression and further collapse of the right lung and or trachea. At the level of   C4, there is a right lateral epidural mass. Several abnormal   appearing cervical lymph nodes are also identified.      The current MRI study demonstrates no change in the size or extent of   the mass. The mass enhances with the contrast material. The mass is   present bilaterally within the C1-C2, C2-C3, and C3-C4 neural   foramina, and wraps around the C2 and C3 vertebrae anteriorly.   Prominent prevertebral tissue at the C2 level narrows the   oropharyngeal airway. As on the CT scan, there is no definite erosion   of the cortex of the bone. Although the spinal cord is not displaced   or distorted by the mass, there is significant exclusion of CSF from   the space around the spinal cord at the level of the C2 inferior   endplate, effectively resulting in severe spinal stenosis.      Additional lesions are identified within the T1, T2, and T4 vertebral   bodies. Additional lesions are also identified in several vertebrae, not   apparent on the comparison CT study.      5.  The above lesions are all concerning for metastases from known   metastatic cervical cancer.      6.  Mild degenerative findings involve several levels in the cervical   spine. Ms.  X  is a 44-year-old African-American female with HPV-related (p16+) SCC of the cervix with metastatic spread to the lungs.  She was initially diagnosed in 2016 following presenting with post-coital bleeding and was found to have Stage 1B1 disease with positive lymphovascular space and deep stromal invasion.  She was initially treated with concurrent chemoradiation with cisplatin and pelvic-targeted XRT with no evidence of disease. She developed disease recurrence with metastatic spread in March 2019 with bulky mediastinal and hilar adenopathy with bilateral pulmonary parenchymal nodules.  Initiation of C1 of carboplatin + taxol was complicated by the development of right and left mainstem bronchus obstruction requiring left-sided bronchial stent placement. She underwent palliative radiation to the lungs and mediastinum followed by reinitiation of carboplatin + taxol x 9 cycles with progression of disease. She then completed single-agent topotecan x 6 cycles with progression of disease in Jan 2020. Stephanie Amika  X  is a 44-year-old African-American female with HPV-related (p16+) metastatic SCC of the cervix with metastatic spread to the lungs.  She was initially diagnosed in 2016 following presenting with post-coital bleeding and was found to have Stage 1B1 disease with positive lymphovascular space and deep stromal invasion.  She was initially treated with concurrent chemoradiation with cisplatin and pelvic-targeted XRT with no evidence of disease. She developed disease recurrence with metastatic spread in March 2019 with bulky mediastinal and hilar adenopathy with bilateral pulmonary parenchymal nodules.  Initiation of C1 of carboplatin + taxol was complicated by the development of right and left mainstem bronchus obstruction requiring left-sided bronchial stent placement. She underwent palliative radiation to the lungs and mediastinum followed by reinitiation of carboplatin + taxol x 9 cycles with progression of disease. Most recently, she completed single-agent topotecan x 6 cycles with progression of disease in Jan 2020.

04/15/16. Presented with abnormal uterine bleeding. Underwent Pap and HPV testing. Pap smear significant for atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance (ASCUS). Hight-risk HPV assay positive.
04/27/16. Underwent colposcopy. Pathology showed invasive moderately-to-poorly differentiated squamous cell carcinoma. Tumor cells noted to be positive for p16, p40, and CK 5/6.
05/10/16. PET/CT showed a focus of hypermetabolic uptake in the cervix (SUV 13); two nodes in the bilateral groin were noted to have mild, non-specific FDG uptake. Staging 1b1 (T1b1N0M0).

05/27/16. Underwent laparoscopic radical abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salphingectomy and pelvic lymph node dissection. Pathology showed positive lymphovascular space invasion with deep stromal invasion. Negative lymph nodes.
07/08/16. Concurrent cisplatin x 5 cycles and XRT 4500 cGy to the pelvis; completed August 2016.
11/08/16. PET/CT with no evidence of disease.
Oct 2018. Developed an upper respiratory infection with cough. Her cough lingered and then became progressive. Shortness of breath was noted in Jan 2019.

03/29/19. Presented to the ED with hemoptysis. PET/CT showed new metastatic disease, with bulky mediastinal and hilar adenopathy with bilateral pulmonary parenchymal nodules. No FDG avid disease below the diaphragm.

04/05/19. EBUS noted a large tumor at the carina. L mainstem bronchus was approximately 90% occluded and the R mainstem broncus was approximately 50% occluded. Biopsy pathology showed p16-positive squamous cell carcinoma.

04/07/19. Started palliative chemotherapy with carboplatin + taxol. Following one cycle of therapy, she developed worsening shortness of breath. CT chest showed interval development of L mainstem bronchus occlusion secondary to necrotic tissue and mucous. She underwent bronch with L mainstem bronchus stent placement.

04/23/19. Presented again with respiratory decompensation due to complete obstruction of the L mainstem bronchus by mucous and 80% obstruction of the R mainstem bronchus by bleeding tumor. Tumor was debulked as much as possible but limited by patient's ventilation.
04/30/19. Palliative radiation, 3000 cGy to the lungs and mediastinum. Bronchus stent was removed.
05/01/19. Tumor molecular profile analysis from carinal excision. MSI-stable. Low TMB score. Low PDL1 expression score.
10/16/19. PET/CT showed progression of disease; with improved bilateral paramediastinal opacities but with interval development of R paratracheal and hilar hypermetabolic adenopathy
01/15/20. Report unavailable, but patient reports progression of disease by imaging.
- Hemoptysis, intermittent, with minimal blood noted.
Appetite - fair, 6kg weight loss in the past 6 weeks
Cough - intermittently productive of white/clear sputum, using q4h duonebs and tessalon perls.
DOE - stable, able to do ADLs
Central chest pain, controlled on Morphine ER 45mg every 12 hours and morphine 15mg IR (4x/day)

column2: Agree with assessment and plan of Dr Burkitt. Ms  X  comes to clinic today for Day 15 of NHSIL12. Overall she reports she tolerated treatment relatively well since only some mild fevers (Tmax 102.5) as well as some daily sensation of warmth. Temperatures have been running in 99s but no other fevers. She reported some associated chills with the 102.5 temp that occurred 3 days after the injection. She also reports possibly worsening of her baseline cough. She is known to have a Left bronchial mass that previously causes compression of her left main bronchus. She had a prior bronchial stent placed in 4/2019 per review of her records. When asked about the breathing and coughing, she said she wasnt sure if it actually worsened or if she just focused on it more. She reports improvement with albuterol neb. Denies mucus production or DOE. She reports she had been coughing at night which interrupted sleep prior to the treatment, but now is sleeping though the night after the use of the neb. Clinically she looked well and she maintained her O2 sat > 90% on ambulation. In listening to her lungs today on clinical exam, she did have bronchial breath sounds in left upper lung, no crackles or rales. Very end expiratory wheezes were present. D/w PI Dr Gulley. Will proceed with treatment today.  D/w Radiology (see my prior note) at time of visit and then discussed with Dr Reed following completion of clinic. There was disagreement on if there truly is a new opacity in left apex. However, both Dr Malayeri and Dr Reed felt this was likely due to volume loss potentially due to radiation changes and/or tumor growth. There was no evidence of pneumonia or a consolidation. No new pleural effusions. Will have pulmonary see her at next visit given her history of a prior bronchial stent. Will also plan for early restaging at next visit in 2 weeks with CT CAP.

Agree with assessment and plan by Dr Chau. Briefly Mr Neves comes to clinic today for week 13 of HPV Trap protocol. Overall he is feeling well with minimal complaints. At last visit, his LFTs were noted to be increased. Treatment was held at that time. Repeat labs last week at his PCP showed continued increase in LFTs. Labs today with further increase in LFTs (AST = 187 = 4.6xULN; ALT =197 = 4.8xULN; both grade 2 elevations). This is possibly due to M7824 treatment. However, today Mr Neves reports using Tumeric to help with his joint inflammation. He was instructed to stop this asap as this could contribute to his LFT elevation. Due to progression LFT elevation, he was started on Prednisone 40mg daily today. He will have his LFTs checked at home again next week. If improved, we will taper his steroids at that time. It is unclear at this time if his LFTs are due to M7824 or tumeric. Due to his DM, he was instructed to contact his endocrinologist today in the event his insulin needed to be adjusted. Mr Neves also continues to have TSH elevation. His synthryoid dose was increased at the last visit - CTM for now.   Mr Neves had restaging scans today. Per my measurements, his target lesions are SD per RECIST but have increased approx 15% from baseline (specifically target lesion #2). A few other nontarget lesions have increased in size as well. The CT read indicates progression but I do not think it meets PD per recist. We will await formal tumor measurements. Today I discussed with him that it is unclear at this time if his tumor is growing (maybe minimal growth) but we will continue to hold treatment at this time due to his LFT elevation. Will check labs next week and taper prednisone as appropriate.  RTC 2 weeks.
Lab addendum: TB is normal is setting of elevated AST/ALT.

- Patient was admitted at the NIH clinical center 1/21-28/2020 for cholecystitis requiring open cholecystectomy on 1/23; she was also found to have spontaneous right pneumothorax requiring pigtail catheter (placed 1/22, removed 1/28); additionally, she underwent IR biliary drain exchange
- After discharge she had poor appetite and nausea/vomiting

- Since discharge, appetite and energy have improved; last low-grade fever was before this past weekend; more discomfort than pain around biliary drain site and stiffness from limited movement.  Spending most of the day up, but not very physically active.
- Mild epistaxis (only with blowing nose) continues, but improved from before

- Sep 2015: Abnormal pap smear led to colposcopy, followed by LEEP; diagnosed with FIGO stage IB1 SCC of the cervix

Pathology not definitive; underwent re-biopsy on Jan 19, 2018, which confirmed recurrent SCC

- Feb 15, 2018 PET-CT: Soft tissue posterior to the urinary bladder described 1/5/18 CT image not hypermetabolic.  Moderate R hydronephrosis of which the etiology is not clear; however there is probably obstruction in the region of the right ureterovesical junction.
- Feb 2018, recommended chemoradiation with proton therapy and then interstitial brachytherapy, however her insurance company denied proton therapy.

- Apr 12, 2018: external beam pelvic radiation therapy (total dose of 50.4 Gy)and received concurrent weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m2 IV chemotherapy X 5 cycles, completing treatment on 5/21/18; tolerated well. She did report diarrhea at the time consistent with radiation proctitis due to the scatter from the radiation, but those have since resolved. Subsequent MRI pelvis which revealed excellent response.

- June 13, 2018: OR by Dr. Rao and Dr. Nichols (Univ of Maryland) for pelvic EUA/laparoscopic lysis of adhesions/placement of interstitial implant for HDR brachytherapy.  Completed interstitial brachytherapy (EQD2 total dose of > 75 Gy) and discharged home on 6/15/18.
- Aug 14, 2018: L ureteral stent removed by urology

1. Improved vaginal cuff thickening compared to pre-treatment imaging, compatible with treatment response; mild residual thickening along the superior aspect of the cuff is nonspecific. There is no mass-like enhancement or diffusion restriction to suggest residual/recurrent tumor. 2. No pelvic lymphadenopathy. 3. Scarring along and adjacent to the cuff involving the distal ureters with mild ureteral dilation, left greater than right

An ultrasound showed intraductal hepatic dilation and a mass.  CT scan on 6/10/19 showed an ill-defined suspicious appearing 3 cm mass-like area near the porta hepatis with enhancement characteristics suspicious for cholangiocarcinoma (see below). MRCP which revealed biliary obstruction. ERCP which revealed near complete obstruction at the porta hepatis. Additionally, recurrent left hydronephrosis was noted and urology was consulted and left ureteral stent was placed.  Of note, she had a UTI, for which she received IV antibiotics.

Assessment: 48 year-old female with metastatic SCC of the cervix, currently with disease involving porta hepatis and right liver, currently on clinical trial of M7824.  She has measurable disease in right liver lobe. She also has known left hydronephrosis and a ureteral stent from a previously irradiated soft tissue lesion (not FDG avid). She also has bilateral biliary drains in place, which were originally placed in 6/2019 due to obstruction from the porta hepatis mass resulting hyperbilirubinemia. This has also been complicated by Enterobacter and Klebsiella bacteremia in early 8/2019, for which she took a 14 day course of PO ciprofloxacin (completed on 8/11/2019), as well as multiple issues with biliary drain malfunctions.  She started Week 1 of M7824 on 8/6/2019. Since then, she has developed a grade 1 rash (confined to her forearms bilaterally) and some gingival bleeding with slight anemia.  She has also developed a grade 2 transaminitis (ALT elevation >AST elevation) and week 3, 5, and 7 treatments were held. She has now completed palliative XRT to porta hepatis lesion (5 sessions, end 10/1) and bilateral biliary drains were successfully internalized. Had L ureteral stent exchange and R placed by urology.  She was admitted to NIH Clinical Center 1/21-28/2020 for cholecystectomy for cholecystitis, pigtail catheter for spontaneous right pneumothorax, and IR biliary drain exchange.  Subsequently, she was admitted to UPMC 2/17-25/2020 for urosepsis leading to fungemia and has completed treatment with antibiotics/anti-fungals (ureteral stents exchanged).  Since then, while her energy and appetite have improved, here weight continues to trend down.  ECOG 2  On restaging imaging, there is interval increase in size of perihepatic, bladder and pelvic masses.  The patient has been deemed to have progression of disease (radiographic progression of non-target lesions) and, as such, has been taken off-treatment.  The patient had molecular testing done on lesions removed during her cholecystectomy and there were no actionable mutations found.  The patient will return to her outside oncologist (Dr. Misas), with whom she met recently, and discuss next treatment options, including standard chemotherapy and ipi/nivo.  We also discussed with the patient that there may be a future iteration of this clinical trial that the patient could be screened for in a few months when the trial opens.  # Metastatic SCC of cervix: C1D1 of M7824 8/6/19; last treatment was week 23. Assessment: 48 year-old female with metastatic SCC of the cervix, currently with disease involving porta hepatis and right liver, currently on clinical trial of M7824.  She has measurable disease in right liver lobe. She also has known left hydronephrosis and a ureteral stent from a previously irradiated soft tissue lesion (not FDG avid). She started Week 1 of M7824 on 8/6/2019. Since then, she has developed a grade 1 rash (confined to her forearms bilaterally) and some gingival bleeding with slight anemia.  She has also developed a grade 2 transaminitis (ALT elevation >AST elevation) and week 3, 5, and 7 treatments were held. She has now completed palliative XRT to porta hepatis lesion (5 sessions, end 10/1) and bilateral biliary drains were successfully internalized. Had L ureteral stent exchange and R placed by urology.  Today she presents for week 19 evaluation and looks and feels well. She is eating and drinking well and labs today notable improved transaminitis. Imaging notable for new liver lesion. We will proceed with treatment today and plan for repeat evaluation with staging scans in 6 wks. 48F with FIGO stage IB1 squamous cell cervical cancer diagnosed in 2015, s/p  radical hysterectomy/bilateral salpingectomy/bilateral pelvic lymphadenectomy (ovary sparing), with local recurrence in 1/2018 treated with definitive concurrent chemoradiation therapy using cisplatin as radiosensitizer. She developed hyperbilirubinemia secondary to biliary obstruction from metastatic disease to the liver in 4/2019, confirmed to be squamous cell carcinoma.
Reason for visit: restaging scans and evaluation prior to Week 13

Saw urologist at the end of last week and have L ureteral stent exchanged, new on right. One dime sized blood clot in urine last week (pre-procedure), none other. Occasional gum bleeding (especially if flossing teeth). Mild epistaxis if blows nose. Gets night sweats, stable (predated treatment). Stable scattered bumps over upper back. Occasionally itchy. No urinary issues aside from blood as described above. Stable hemorrhoid, no bleeding. Dropped a couple # but had to fast a couple times for tests. LEE resolved.
- Sep 2015: Abnormal pap smear led to colposcopy, followed by LEEP; diagnosed with FIGO stage IB1 SCC of the cervix

- Sept 2015: Robot-assisted laparoscopic radical hysterectomy/bilateral salpingectomy/bilateral pelvic lymphadenectomy; final pathology at the time revealed SCC, grade 3 with cervical stroma invasion (8mm), LVSI, negative margins, with 0/11 R nodes involved and 0/18 left nodes involved; no adjuvant therapy

- Jan 2018: developed LLE swelling – Doppler negative, but CT of A/P 1/15/2018 showed L hydronephrosis with obstruction by a soft tissue mass (5.4 cm x 3.5 cm); Subsequently underwent a biopsy of the vaginal cuff, cystoscopy and L ureteral stent placement; procedure revealed that the vaginal cuff was indurated, but not involved and no bladder lesions.  Pathology at the time was not definitive; underwent another biopsy on Jan 19, 2018, which confirmed recurrent SCC

- Feb 15, 2018 PET-CT: Soft tissue posterior to the urinary bladder described 1/5/18 CT image not hypermetabolic.  Moderate R hydronephrosis of which the etiology is not entirely clear; however there is probably obstruction in the region of the right ureterovesical junction.
- Feb 2018, she was recommended to undergo chemoradiation with proton therapy and then interstitial brachytherapy, however her insurance company denied proton therapy.

- Apr 12, 2018: began external beam pelvic radiation therapy (total dose of 50.4 Gy)and received concurrent weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m2 IV chemotherapy X 5 cycles, completing treatment on 5/21/18; tolerated well. She did report having some symptoms (diarrhea) at the time consistent with radiation proctitis due to the scatter from the radiation, but those have since resolved. Subsequent MRI pelvis which revealed excellent response.

- June 13, 2018: OR by Dr. Rao and Dr. Nichols (Univ of Maryland) for pelvic EUA/laparoscopic lysis of adhesions/placement of interstitial implant for HDR brachytherapy.  Completed interstitial brachytherapy (EQD2 total dose of > 75 Gy) and discharged home on 6/15/18.
- Aug 14, 2018: L ureteral stent removed by urology

1. Improved vaginal cuff thickening compared to pre-treatment imaging, compatible with treatment response; mild residual thickening along the superior aspect of the cuff is nonspecific. There is no mass-like enhancement or diffusion restriction to suggest residual/recurrent tumor. 2. No pelvic lymphadenopathy. 3. Scarring along and adjacent to the cuff involving the distal ureters with mild ureteral dilation, left greater than right

- April 2019-June 2019: patient doing well until she became febrile ~2-3 weeks apart in April-May 2019; she visited her primary care physician and labs were done, noted for abnormal LFTs; she was admitted to UPMC Pinnacle from 6/10/19 – 6/14/19 for transaminitis and hyperbilirubinemia.  An ultrasound showed intraductal hepatic dilation and a mass.  CT scan on 6/10/19 showed an ill-defined suspicious appearing 3 cm mass-like area near the porta hepatis with enhancement characteristics suspicious for cholangiocarcinoma (see below).  She underwent an MRCP which revealed biliary obstruction.  She then underwent an ERCP which revealed near complete obstruction at the porta hepatis.  She had bilateral biliary drains placed by IR and since then, here transaminitis and hyperbilirubinemia have improved.  At the time, she had an IR biopsy of the obstructing lesion at the porta hepatis, which showed SCC.  Additionally, recurrent left hydronephrosis was noted and urology was consulted and left ureteral stent was placed.  Of note, she had a UTI, for which she received IV antibiotics.

- CT A/P 6/10/19: Impression: 1. Interval development of market biliary ductal dilation in both lobes of the liver with ill-defined suspicious appearing 3 cm masslike area near the porta hepatis with enhancement characteristics suspicious for cholangiocarcinoma; metastatic disease cannot be excluded. 2. Persistent hydronephrosis and marked hydroureter on the left terminating at perviously described ill-defined masslike fullness in the pelvis at the vaginal cuff; differential considerations include residual or recurrent neoplasm as well as postoperative scarring. A 1 mm distal left ureteral stone cannot be excluded.
- June 13, 2018 - Liver lesion biopsy: Fibrous tissue with squamous cell carcinoma; no hepatocytes can be identified; High-risk HPV subtypes 16/18 detected

-PET-CT 6/27/19: Impression: 1. Intense area of metabolic activity in the region of the porta hepatis near the catheter 2. Sheetlike area of abnormal tracer uptake in the space between the ribs in the right hepatic lobe. Metastatic disease cannot be excluded
- 7/12/19: Patient underwent internalization and capping of biliary drains.

HEENT: Normacephalic, Pupils equal, round and react to light, Extraocular movements intact, Mouth without erythema, lesions, or exudates, Mucus membranes moist, Oropharnyx clear
Pulmonary: Clear to auscultation bilaterally, No rales, No rhonchi, No wheezing, Good aeration, No accessory muscle use/retractions
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, Normal S1 and S2, No murmurs, No rubs

Assessment: 48 year-old female with metastatic SCC of the cervix, currently with disease involving porta hepatis and right liver, currently on clinical trial of M7824.   She has measurable disease in right liver lobe. She also has known left hydronephrosis and a ureteral stent from a previously irradiated soft tissue lesion (not FDG avid). She also has bilateral biliary drains in place, which were originally placed in 6/2019 due to obstruction from the porta hepatis mass resulting hyperbilirubinemia. This has also been complicated by Enterobacter and Klebsiella bacteremia in early 8/2019, for which she took a 14 day course of PO ciprofloxacin (completed on 8/11/2019), as well as multiple issues with biliary drain malfunctions.   She started Week 1 of M7824 on 8/6/2019. Since then, she has developed a grade 1 rash (confined to her forearms bilaterally) and some gingival bleeding with slight anemia.  She has also developed a grade 2 transaminitis (ALT elevation >AST elevation) and week 3, 5, and 7 treatments were held. She has now completed palliative XRT to porta hepatis lesion (5 sessions, end 10/1) and bilateral biliary drains were successfully internalized. Had L ureteral stent exchange and R placed last week.   Labs today with normal transaminases, normal lipase, improved anemia. No rash over forearms but very subtle occasionally itchy rash on neck/upper back. Stable epistaxis, gingival bleeding, hematuria (difficult to interpret in the setting of recent stent exchange/placement).   Scans today with stable disease.  Proceed with week 13 treatment today.   ECOG 1   # Metastatic SCC of cervix  - C1D1 of M7824 8/6/19  - Weeks 3/5/7 all held of treatment due to grade 2 transaminitis, now resolved  - Will proceed with week 13 treatment today 10/29  - Return to clinic in 2 weeks   # Malignant biliary obstruction s/p biliary drain placement  - Now successfully capped and without issues will f/u with IR for complete internalization  - has appointment 11/18 for follow-up   # Bilateral hydronephrosis, has bilateral ureteral stents  - Cr 1.1 today (slightly improved from last visit) - continue follow-up with urologist

- Sept 2015: Robot-assisted laparoscopic radical hysterectomy/bilateral salpingectomy/bilateral pelvic lymphadenectomy; final pathology at the time revealed SCC, grade 3 with cervical stroma invasion (8mm), LVSI, negative margins, with 0/11 R nodes involved and 0/18 left nodes involved; no adjuvant therapy

- Jan 2018: developed LLE swelling – Doppler negative, but CT of A/P 1/15/2018 showed L hydronephrosis with obstruction by a soft tissue mass (5.4 cm x 3.5 cm); Subsequently underwent a biopsy of the vaginal cuff, cystoscopy and L ureteral stent placement; procedure revealed that the vaginal cuff was indurated, but not involved and no bladder lesions.  Pathology at the time was not definitive; underwent another biopsy on Jan 19, 2018, which confirmed recurrent SCC

- Feb 15, 2018 PET-CT: Soft tissue posterior to the urinary bladder described 1/5/18 CT image not hypermetabolic.  Moderate R hydronephrosis of which the etiology is not entirely clear; however there is probably obstruction in the region of the right ureterovesical junction.  Hydronephrosis from the previous study in the left kidney is no longer visualized; there is a stent in the left ureter.
- Feb 2018, she was recommended to undergo chemoradiation with proton therapy and then interstitial brachytherapy, however her insurance company denied proton therapy.

- Apr 12, 2018: began external beam pelvic radiation therapy (total dose of 50.4 Gy)and received concurrent weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m2 IV chemotherapy X 5 cycles, completing treatment on 5/21/18; tolerated well. She did report having some symptoms (diarrhea) at the time consistent with radiation proctitis due to the scatter from the radiation, but those have since resolved.  Subsequent MRI pelvis which revealed excellent response.

Patient is a 84 year old Female. Current Attending is Dr Strauss.

84-year old exceptionally pleasant woman with a history of locally advanced vulvar cancer diagnosed in November 2017. She initially presented with vaginal bleeding, dysuria and vulvar discomfort. She was found to have locally extensive node-positive, HPV-positive disease which deemed to be unresectable. The vulvar mass was T2 (lower third of the vagina and urethra) N2 (0.7 cm and 1 cm inguinal lymph nodes) MO squamous cell carcinoma of the vulva. The MRI described the mass involving the anterior aspect of the lower third of the vagina in close proximity to the urethra. It also extended posteriorly to involve the perianal body, but there was no involvement of the anal canal or rectum. It measured 4.5 cm in anterior posterior dimension and 5.4 cm along the length of the vagina. There was no evidence of cervical involvement. There were enlarged inguinal lymph nodes on the right side up to 0.7 cm in short axis dimension. There was also an enlarged anterior right iliac lymph node that was 0.9 cm in short axis dimension.

She received external beam radiotherapy with concurrent Cisplatin (2 cycles out of the 5) with no further chemotherapy due to renal failure (thought to be pre-renal). She finished treatment in February 2018. She had a very good response to the  trea tment with complete regression of the lesions. She had follow up MRI of the pelvis on April 25 which showed marked treatment response. There was no evidence of residual mass in the vulva, and the previously noted right inguinal and external iliac lymph nodes were also smaller. On post-treatment exams, there were some superficial plaques close to the introitus and urethra that were attributed to post-radiation changes (March 2018 and April 2018).Per notes, a follow up exam July was consistent with a white plaque-like area along the anterior vaginal wall in the suburethral area and no significant changes from before. There was a small thickened area near the posterior fourchette, just to the right of the midline. This was attributed to post-treatment changes.

She was seen on September 5th, 2018 and reported urinary complaints that she was unable to completely empty her bladder in addition to diarrhea. On exam, there was some equivocal finding in the vagina. Biopsies from the posterior vagina came back as a spindle cell variant of squamous cell carcinoma (sarcomatoid features). Daughter reports that patient PDL-1 was >90% positive. Cystoscopy was done which didn’t show any bladder masses, cytology sent. MRI pelvis done on 10/19/2018. The 1cm focal area of reduced enhancement of the left vagina wall as described is equivocal for a focus of disease. No metastatic disease in the pelvis. CT chest, abdomen and pelvis did not show any evidence of metastatic disease. On 11/6/2018, a PET-scan showed intense metabolic activity in the vagina is consistent with the biopsy proven recurrent/residual malignancy. No PET-CT evidence of nodal or distant metastasis. The previously seen uptake in right inguinal femoral nodes has resolved. The impression was that new vulvar lesion is likely represents recurrence of original carcinoma. However, it was quite a different morphology appearance compared to the original cancer.

Patient met with gynecologic oncology surgeon and radiation oncology and conclusion was not to perform further surgery (b/c LN+ at baseline, and at the time largely asymptomatic) or radiation therapy. However, to consider systematic therapy. Another options would be to consider total exenteration which might be risky given advanced age. She also provided NGS report copy. She had PET-scan 2 weeks ago which was same as previously done in November.
Improved urinary stream. She feels well, has good energy. No dysuria. No urine incontinence. She has good  appetite. No CVS or respiratory sxs.  No GI sxs. nO vaginal bleeding reported.

column2: Patient has been seen with follow in clinic on Tuesday, February 12..  I agree with the follows assessment and plan.  In brief this patient is a 29-year-old female patient with metastatic cervical cancer status post 2 lines of therapy, currently progressing and screening for the clinical trial with M7824.  She met all of the eligibility criteria for this trial, and we started her on with treatment today after obtaining an informed consent.  Review of the patients scans show that her lesions were mostly less than 2.2 cm in largest diameter. She has shown local recurrence along with lung and liver metastases.  The patient has been explained the mechanism of action and potential benefits of the drug along with the side effects in details.  We stressed the fact that we also so potentially increased risk of bleeding in some patients.  Most of these bleedings have been like a platelet like type of bleeding which include gingival bleeding and nose bleeds but at times these beats could be serious.  The patient is currently on anticoagulation for her subsegmental PE, and we explained that this might increase the risk of bleeding further.  The patient initially opted to continue therapy as is with full dose of Lovenox and plan to change to oral anticoagulation later, but later after discussion with Dr. Strauss, the patient opted to go for prophylactic dose of Lovenox (40 mg daily).   The patient also voiced understanding of the increased risk of clotting with the current use of hormone placement.  She was advised to consult with her gynecologist to find other alternatives that do not hold the same risk of thrombosis as hormones.  The patient later in the week consulted with her gynecologist and she was advised to start on Effexor.  Communicating with the patient by email we confirmed that this would be a good option for her, provided that we check her EKG to make sure that she does not have QT prolongation associated with this drug.   In addition the patient has developed a rash that seem to be related to Lovenox with few petechiae.  The patient was advised to watch carefully for any worsening.
