Review of systems otherwise negative. No fevers, chills, sweats. No chest pain, sob, palpitations, lower extremity edema. No nose bleeds or bleeding gums. No urinary complaint

Diagnosed with invasive, moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma of the anus (presumed HPV+) by colonoscopic biopsy on 05/01/2018, performed for several months of abdominal discomfort, rectal pain and constipation.  Post-procedure, on 05/02/2018, she presented to the emergency department because of persistent pain and underwent CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis which demonstrated an approximately 1.2 cm soft tissue density between the rectosigmoid and left pelvic side wall.  Subsequently performed MRI on 05/10/2018 revealed a 2 cm soft tissue lesion in the mid/high mesorectal fat with associated edema and extension from the left lateral rectal serosa to the left pelvic sidewall (no pelvic lymphadenopathy or abdominopelvic disease evident).  PET-CT scan performed on 05/18/2018 demonstrated increased uptake in the left anal wall, ~1.7 cm soft tissue density within the left sacral region abutting the sigmoid colon and suspicious prominent lymph nodes (largest, 0.8 cm), too small to characterize on PET.

With colonoscopic biopsy-confirmed anal squamous cell carcinoma, she was treated with 5-fluorouracil and mitomycin-C (C1D1 06/05/2018) and radiation (54 Gy in 30 fractions, completed 07/16/2018).  During this time, she developed a PICC-associated deep venous thrombosis which was treated with 3 months of enoxaparin.

She was feeling and doing well until 03/2019, when she again developed abdominal discomfort and progressive rectal pain.  PET-CT imaging was performed and showed an intensely FDG-avid irregular nodular soft tissue mass extending from the left perirectal region (max SUV 4.5) and new FDG avid left hepatic lobe (segment III) hypodensity (SUV 2.8).  MRI was also obtained and demonstrated ""focal cholangitis"".  These findings were, per documentation, discussed at  X ' tumor board and the consensus was that the hepatic lesion was not amenable to biopsy.

At this time, patient pursued care at MD Anderson Cancer Center, where MRI was performed on 06/03/2019 and revealed hypoenhancing masses in segment III and II/III.  PET CT scan was performed on 06/13/19 and showed intensely hypermetabolic L perirectal and L hepatic lesions that had increased from 03/2019 imaging.  On 06/07/2019, she underwent ultrasound-guided liver biopsy and CT-guided pelvic mass biopsy, both deep FNA, with both confirming the presence of squamous cell carcinoma on evaluation of pathology.  She began treatment with carboplatin and paclitaxel (C1D1 06/21/2019) and what appears to have been neoadjuvant IMRT/VMAT to the pelvic mass (3900 cGy, 150 cGy per day in 26 fractions, delivered twice daily, 09/09/2019 - 09/25/2019) preceding what sounds like a planned abdominoperineal resection (per patient's report and medical records).

However, she states that surgery was cancelled because repeat imaging (PET CT scan on 11/04/2019) demonstrated disease progression with vascular involvement (interval growth of conglomerate gastrohepatic and porta hepatis lymph nodes with involvement of adjacent vasculature, though pelvic and liver masses were stable in size on CT scan: ""interval development of hypermetabolic left supraclavicular, gastrohepatic and porta hepatis lymphadenopathy, all consistent with disease progression, interval increase in size and metabolic activity of previously demonstrated left hepatic lobe metastatic lesion, also consistent with disease progression, and relatively stable size and metabolic activity of the previously known hypermetabolic left perirectal lesion"").

She then decided to obtain consultation at MedStar Georgetown with Dr. Weinberg regarding potential trials incorporating use of nivolimab +/- ipilimumab. Treatment options, including clinical trial, were discussed and she was, thus, referred to NIH for evaluation for potential eligibility for enrollment into study 2018-C-0056 (M7824 for SCC). She was enrolled in the study. C1W1D1 = 11/27/2019, C1W3D1 = 12/10/19.

On 12/24/2019 she presented to the clinic prior to W5. She had RUQ discomfort and constipation. Labs showed worsening anemia and elevated bilirubin. CT showed obstruction of the biliary duct at the level of the porta hepatis. She was admitted and then transferred to UMD for ERCP, with stent placed in the CBD 4-5 cm stenosis and of the R main system. The patient was discharged home on 12/27. She had constipation on 12/28, then developed hematochezia after miralax. She was evaluated in the day hospital on 12/29, labs showed down-trending Hb (10.3 on 12/24 to 9.1 on 12/29) and improving LFTs. She did not need any treatment.

Reason for Visit:  Patient with metastatic squamous cell cancer of the anus presents for evaluation as referred by Dr. Adrian Murphy at Johns  X  Hospital for potential enrollment into trial 2018-C-0056: ""M7824 in Subjects with HPV-Associated Malignancies"", P.I.: Strauss.

History of Present Illness:  43 year-old female diagnosed with invasive, moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma of the anus (presumed HPV+) by colonoscopic biopsy on 05/01/2018, performed for several months of abdominal discomfort, rectal pain and constipation.  Post-procedure, on 05/02/2018, she presented to the emergency department because of persistent pain and underwent CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis which demonstrated an approximately 1.2 cm soft tissue density between the rectosigmoid and left pelvic side wall.  Subsequently performed MRI on 05/10/2018 revealed a 2 cm soft tissue lesion in the mid/high mesorectal fat with associated edema and extension from the left lateral rectal serosa to the left pelvic sidewall (no pelvic lymphadenopathy or abdominopelvic disease evident).  PET-CT scan performed on 05/18/2018 demonstrated increased uptake in the left anal wall, ~1.7 cm soft tissue density within the left sacral region abutting the sigmoid colon and suspicious prominent lymph nodes (largest, 0.8 cm), too small to characterize on PET.

With colonoscopic biopsy-confirmed anal squamous cell carcinoma, she was treated with 5-fluorouracil and mitomycin-C (C1D1 06/05/2018) and radiation (54 Gy in 30 fractions, completed 07/16/2018).  During this time, she developed a PICC-associated deep venous thrombosis which was treated with 3 months of enoxaparin.

She was feeling and doing well until 03/2019, when she again developed abdominal discomfort and progressive rectal pain.  PET-CT imaging was performed and showed an intensely FDG-avid irregular nodular soft tissue mass extending from the left perirectal region (max SUV 4.5) and new FDG avid left hepatic lobe (segment III) hypodensity (SUV 2.8).  MRI was also obtained and demonstrated ""focal cholangitis"".  These findings were, per documentation, discussed at  X ' tumor board and the consensus was that the hepatic lesion was not amenable to biopsy.

At this time, patient pursued care at MD Anderson Cancer Center, where MRI was performed on 06/03/2019 and revealed hypoenhancing masses in segment III and II/III.  PET CT scan was performed on 06/13/19 and showed intensely hypermetabolic L perirectal and L hepatic lesions that had increased from 03/2019 imaging.  On 06/07/2019, she underwent ultrasound-guided liver biopsy and CT-guided pelvic mass biopsy, both deep FNA, with both confirming the presence of squamous cell carcinoma on evaluation of pathology.  She began treatment with carboplatin and paclitaxel (C1D1 06/21/2019) and what appears to have been neoadjuvant IMRT/VMAT to the pelvic mass (3900 cGy, 150 cGy per day in 26 fractions, delivered twice daily, 09/09/2019 - 09/25/2019) preceding what sounds like a planned abdominoperineal resection (per patient's report and medical records).

However, she states that surgery was cancelled because repeat imaging (PET CT scan on 11/04/2019) demonstrated disease progression with vascular involvement (interval growth of conglomerate gastrohepatic and porta hepatis lymph nodes with involvement of adjacent vasculature, though pelvic and liver masses were stable in size on CT scan: ""interval development of hypermetabolic left supraclavicular, gastrohepatic and porta hepatis lymphadenopathy, all consistent with disease progression, interval increase in size and metabolic activity of previously demonstrated left hepatic lobe metastatic lesion, also consistent with disease progression, and relatively stable size and metabolic activity of the previously known hypermetabolic left perirectal lesion"").

She then decided to obtain consultation at MedStar Georgetown with Dr. Weinberg regarding potential trials incorporating use of nivolimab +/- ipilimumab. Treatment options, including clinical trial, were discussed and she was, thus, referred to NIH for evaluation for potential eligibility for enrollment into study 2018-C-0056 (M7824 for SCC).

Assessment: Ms. X is a 48 y/o female with metastatic HPV positive vaginal cancer who returns to NIH for week restaging visit on protocol 18-c-0056. She started treatment on 9/18/18 and received a total of 2 doses of M7824 (last dose 10/2/18) with a PR/CR; treatment is being held due to GI bleed and duodenitis could be related to M7824. This was followed by a steroid taper.   Currently she comes q2weeks for follow up. Her subsequent course had been complicated by lower extremity lymphedema, weakness and pain. EMG performed on 1/17 showed evidence of neurogenic injury in L2, L3, L4 muscle distribution. Presence of distal neuropathy was unable to be excluded. The etiology of her weakness and lymphedema remains unclear. Although immune-related process is possible it is unlikely given the timing of events. Since she had radiation to the pelvis, radiation-related nerve injury is also possible. Neurology and radiation oncology are actively following. Empiric course of steroids have been previously discussed. There is concern that since she has received 2 doses of immunotherapy, there is a risk that steroids may dampen the cytotoxic immune effect on the tumor. Neurology and physical therapy suggest that a steroid course may be warranted given continued/progressive lower extremity weakness.   In terms of her disease, PET scan from 1/23/2019 shows ongoing CR.
# Metastatic Vaginal Squamous cell carcinoma, HPV positive
- M7824 on 18-C-0056, C1D1 9/18/18, currently on hold since 10/2/18 for GI bleeding and duodenitis
- Achieved CR with 2 doses, PET scan on 1/23 without active disease
# Lower extremity weakness, bilateral proximal leg weakness (L2-L4)
- Etiology unclear and may be related to radiation-induced neuropathy vs. diabetic myopathy vs. steroid induced myopathy  vs immune-related myopathy.
- CRP previously elevated however has down normalized (coincides with timing of port removal)

- Was seen by Neurology on 2/8/19 who agreed that etiology was unclear. Based on their recommendations will check AchR antibodies. Also recommended that trial of immune suppressant should be considered including either Prednisone or IVIG (2g/kg over 5 days)
- Stopped Gabapentin trial due to GI intolerance
- Will start trial of Prednisone 20mg daily for 2 weeks (quantity of 30 tabs)
- Given Aleve use and new prednisone prescription, will prescribe Protonix 40mg daily
- followed by lymphedema team, continue therapy 2x/week
- MRI of right shoulder inflammation without evidence of rotator cuff tear

Scott David X is a 57-year-old gentleman with squamous cell cancer (p16+, initially T2N1) of the base of tongue, diagnosed 3/2018, now with likely metastatic disease who presents for continued screening for 18-C-0056.

Initial presentation with URI symptoms in January of 2018 associated with bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy. The left cervical LAN resolved while the right side persisted. In March 2018, he was evaluated at  Kaiser (San Diego CA) and an FNA of the  right cervical node was ""suspicious for invasive SCC.""  In April 2018, a CT neck showed enlarged right  posterior submandibular node and soft tissue asymmetry in the right vallecula. Pet Scan 4/27/18  then revealed FDG avid (SUV 10.5) right submandibular node, asymmetric fullness at right base of tongue (SUV 6.8) and a sub centimeter left sided level 2B node (SUV 2.8). Ultimately in June  2018, he underwent laryngoscopic biopsy of right base tongue which confirmed moderately differentiated invasive squamous cell cancer, p16+, T2N1.  He was recommended to undergo definitive chemoRT at Kaiser, and obtained a treatment opinion at Sloan Kettering which concurred with the recommendation for definitive chemoRT. Patient states that he was  not  comfortable with potential side effects of ChemoRT and wanted to try alternative therapies first. He received high dose vitamin C treatments and ozone therapy in the later half of 2018.  In December 2018, a PET scan showed his local disease was ""larger and more aggressive.""  He subsequently presented for treatment at an Integrative oncology treatment center in Reno Nevada where he received low dose chemotherapy (5Fu/cisplatin) with insulin potentiation treatments twice weekly for three weeks, alternating with high dose supplements from February to March  2018. He received 2 additional treatments in April and May 2018, receiving a total of 8 low dose chemo treatments.  He tolerated treatments well with no side effects. He has not received radiation therapy. There has been no imaging to establish status of disease since December 2018.

column2: Patient was seen with the fellow in clinic.  The patient has been off therapy because of aggressive keratoacanthoma/squamous cell carcinoma of the skin secondary to M7824.  She continues to do well clinically at this point except for few medical conditions as mentioned in the note.  Given her history of osteoporosis and uninvolved fracture in her right foot, we considered giving her bisphosphonates.  The patient has seen a dentist and she was supposed to do further workup.  She initially said she needed only minor procedures as filling, but this visit she said that the bone and jaws has been felt to be weak and she might need further treatments.  We have not received any update from her dentist before this visit.  We called the dentist office Dr. Olga Galindo (phone #5617212525), and we await follow-up from their office with an email attaching a report of the dental assessment.  We have not received this today.  That being said, we hold off on bisphosphonates for now until we get a better understanding what is needed to be done by dentist before we go forward with treatment. We will continue to hold off immunotherapy with M78244 now.  Her restaging today has shown stable disease.  Her disease is mainly in the lung.  The lesion that has been irradiated in the past is still very well controlled (almost completely gone).  We had discussions of future planning if the patient were to recurr, to consider compassionate use of immune checkpoint inhibition with avelumab alone without the TG beta part. The patient has been counseled on bleeding risk with M7824 which is mainly mucocutaneous on observation with other patients treated with this drug.  The patient has denied any bleeding events.
Her vitamin D level was checked and it came back at 23 which means she is not deficient.

Patient is a 59 year old Female. Current Attending is Dr. Abdul Sater.
Ms. X is a 59-year-old female from Florida with metastatic squamous cell carcinoma of the anus who presents for week 21 on protocol 18-C-0056.

She initially presented in 2016 with rectal bleeding to the ER at Good Samaritan Medical Center.  She was diagnosed with hemorrhoids and in 5/2016 was referred by another physician who performed noted mass on digital rectal exam.  CT AP 5/15/16 showed an exophytic mass in the posterior aspect of the rectum measuring 2.8 x 2.5 cm.   Colonoscopy by GI (Dr. Urban) 5/23/16 showed anal nodule, internal hemorrhoids, and ileocecal valve polyp, and she was referred to Dr. Larry Sands colorectal surgery at University of Miami for resection of the nodule.  Rectal exam under anesthesia and excision/biopsy on 6/14/16 showed an extensive mass extending from dentate line distally to the anal verge in the right posterior anal canal.  ""It appeared that the sphincter muscle underlying may be involved... this was biopsied and not a full excision."" Pathology revealed invasive anal squamous cell carcinoma (basaloid) within the right posterior anal canal with positive lateral resected margins, lymphovascular invasion, and IHC positive for p16 within tumor cells.  She was staged as Stage T2, N0, M0.  PET/CT 7/1/16 showed ""focal intense uptake in the anus.""

She received systemic 5FU/mitomycin/RT (7/11/16-8/19/16) for local disease at Florida Cancer Specialists under Dr. Peles.  Treatment complicated by severe radiation dermatitis and lymphedema in bilateral legs and feet with 2-week inpatient hospitalization.
She was disease-free per PET/CT (11/28/16) and CT CAP scan (10/10/16).

She developed lung mets in 12/2017, with multiple new bilateral pulmonary nodules compatible with metastatic disease per CT CAP on 12/18/17 and by PET/CT (hypermetabolic pulm nodules).  CT-guided biopsy of the right lung nodule core biopsy on 1/9/18 showed poorly differentiated carcinoma c/w metastatic basaloid squamous carcinoma (P16 strongly positive).

Several months later, after she was told she had ""6 months to live,"" she sought second opinion at the Cleveland Clinic in Florida and was treated with cisplatin + 5 FU (3/5/18) for metastatic disease, but developed a severe reaction ~ 18 hours into infusion (unsure if secondary to Cisplatin or 5FU), and was considered intolerant to this chemo and has had no treatment since.

During 2018, she developed significant low back pain and pain in upper thighs, MRI of spine showed no metastatic disease, but did show degenerative disc disease and was suffering from radiation induced neuropathy.
She enrolled on NCI protocol 18-c-0056 and received her first treatment with M7824 on 6/19/18.

Restaging scans show increase in size of lesion to about 7 cm with necrosis.  Paraspinal lesion was biopsied and consistent with metastatic SCC.  She was admitted and received palliative XRT to the lesion for 10 days (30 Gy in 10 fractions completed 9/21).

column2: Patient was evaluated by me in OP12 clinic on 04 Dec 2018. She reports that the excisional shave biopsy site on the left forearm is healing without complication.  She continues to have multiple KA lesions on the chest arms and legs that bother her. There may have been some regression in a few older lesions, but she also reports new lesions on the arms. If the patient goes back on M7824, will consider treating with acitretin. Pruritus improved with change off morphine.  Patient can continue to use topical steroids from symptomatic control. R/B/A of chronic steroids discussed. Continue Sarna PRN. Unclear if the patient is getting benefit from aprepitant and antihistamines. If patient can obtain topical cream containing TGFb she can start treating a test site. If not, we can start a trial of topical retinoids.

Assessment: Mr. X is a 49 year old male with HPV35+ metastatic squamous cell carcinoma of the left tonsil. Patient was initially diagnosed in January 2017 with Stage IVa (T2N2M0) disease. He completed seven-weeks of radiation therapy with concurrent cisplatinum (30 mg/m2 weekly) with initial response in July 2017. However, by November 2017, imaging showed progression of disease with disease noted by PET/CT in the R palantine tonsil, R maxillary soft tissue, L neck soft tissue, and superior mediastinal lymph nodes. When he was attempting to start immunotherapy, lesions were noted to have spontaneously regressed below size cut-off of 2.5 cm diameter. He pursued alternative medicines, including THC-based oils and extracts, but was followed with intermittent serial imaging. In Sept 2019, patient was noted to have interval increase of RML lung lesion and new chest and abdomen lymphadenopathy concerning for metastatic disease. Patient has been off therapy since Nov 2017. He presents to clinic today for initiation of treatment with protocol 18-c-0056.   Most recent imaging (10/16/19) shows no local disease recurrence in the neck but multiple new and enlarging areas of possible metastatic disease in the chest and abdomen. Patient had CT done one week ago which did show some increase in the size of subcarinal lymph nodes and some ground glass opacities in the lungs. Possibilities include disease progression with lymphangitic spread vs Pneumonitis. Patient has took prednisone 40 mg for five days with some improvement in his sob day 3-5. Patient did not understand that he should have continued the Prednisone 20 mg along with the Flovent. He has not been using the inhalers because of tachycardia ( heart rate with albuterol 180) even with the Flovent. He now feels the same way he did last week prior to starting the steroids. Given he is having oxygen saturations of 80 on exertion on home, we will restage him today. We will also get pulmonary consult for further input into the etiology.    Regarding his UA with some blood, patient has a history of a kidney stone. He denied any urinary symptoms.   His TSH is elevated today at 11.05. This is likely due to the immunotherapy. We will start him on Thyroxine 50mcg daily in the am 30 mins before meals.  He also has a transaminitis, which is slightly worse than before.

-Will restage today with CT chest abdomen and pelvis
-Shortness of breath on exertion etiology remains unclear of disease progression vs Pneumonitis.
-We will determine further management plan after he has the CT restaging.
-Start Thyroxine 50mcg oral once daily 30 mins before breakfast

column2: Saw Mr X today with Mr Carter and agree with her plan with following comments. Due to a misunderstanding of directions, Mr X took only one dose of prednisone 20 mg, and then he also discontinued the inhaled GC, consequently he feels overall worse today in terms of fatigue and dyspnea. Pulse oximetry at home reportedly down to 80% occasionally, however without dizziness and in the context of tachycardia, maybe a spuriously low read. On physical exam the kyphoscoliosis confounds the assessment of symmetry of respiratory sounds. In all, we will proceed with CT chest today, and obtain a pulmonary consultation.  In addition, there is a continuing increase in TSH with normal FT4, which may represent immune thyroiditis on the radiation-induced thyroid dysfunction, and we will start thyroxine supplementation 50mcg. The LFT elevation may represent immune AE, and therefore we will hold treatment today and prescribe low-dose prednisone (0.5 mg/kg/d = 40 mg/d), which will also be helping the dyspnea. In addition to the CT chest we will be obtaining full imaging assessment. His microscopic hematuria is unaccompanied by symptoms or WBCs, and he reports recurrent episodes of such microscopic hematuria caused by his pre-existing urolithiasis.
Per recommendation of Pulmonary Consult we will be obtaining nasal wash and induced sputum today, and we have made appointments for ECHO, PFTs (incl. DLCO) and 6MWT on 12/17.

Radiology notifies us that CT scans today are cancelled due to both CT scanners not working, and will be possibly operational tomorrow. We discussed with Mr X and will be falling back to the plan for CT scans on 12/17, unless results from respiratory tests today or interim events dictate necessity for earlier scans.

Assessment: Mr. X is a 49 year old male with HPV35+ metastatic squamous cell carcinoma of the left tonsil. Patient was initially diagnosed in January 2017 with Stage IVa (T2N2M0) disease. He completed seven-weeks of radiation therapy with concurrent cisplatinum (30 mg/m2 weekly) with initial response in July 2017. However, by November 2017, imaging showed progression of disease with disease noted by PET/CT in the R palantine tonsil, R maxillary soft tissue, L neck soft tissue, and superior mediastinal lymph nodes. When he was attempting to start immunotherapy, lesions were noted to have spontaneously regressed below size cut-off of 2.5 cm diameter. He pursued alternative medicines, including THC-based oils and extracts, but was followed with intermittent serial imaging. In Sept 2019, patient was noted to have interval increase of RML lung lesion and new chest and abdomen lymphadenopathy concerning for metastatic disease. Patient has been off therapy since Nov 2017. He presents to clinic today for initiation of treatment with protocol 18-c-0056.   Most recent imaging (10/16/19) shows no local disease recurrence in the neck but multiple new and enlarging areas of possible metastatic disease in the chest and abdomen. He has completed concurrent radiation/cisplatin in 2017 but is otherwise treatment naive and is most interested in avoiding additional chemotherapy. We discussed protocol 18-c-0056 with the patient and his wife, including potential side effects, and patient was amenable to starting therapy today.    # Metastatic squamous cell carcinoma of the L tonsil. HPV 35+.  - Patient consented for initiation of protocol 18-c-0056 at todays visit  - Contraception was discussed with the patient and his wife and he was agreeable to using contraception during therapy - C1D1 today. Will administer pre-medications with tylenol and benadryl followed by flat-dose M7824 as per protocol

column2: Called to oncology clinic to evaluate new papules on the skin.  Patient was seen two weeks ago with pruritus and a few keratotic papules that could have represented early KAs. Patient is back today with multiple additional keratotic papules - some of which are tender. Most of the lesions are on the bilateral legs, but some on the arms as well.  The patient reports improvement in her pruritus related to use of hydroxyzine that she takes in the evening. The topical steroids do not help as much. The patient notes she once again traveled to the caribbean since the last visit. She sometimes burns and always tans. On exam today the patient is very tan. She has multiple 2-4mm keratotic papules on the bilateral legs and a few on the arms. Some are excoriated. There is at least one on the left lateral calf that is tender and presents as a domed papule with a keratotic core. There are excoriated small papules on the back. The patient has multiple (10-15) lesions concerning for keratoacanthomas with at least one that is clinically classic for KA. Of note, this is week 11 on M7824 and this is quite early for KA onset. The patient is not getting M7824 today as she shows disease progression. The patient requests treatment of the symptomatic lesions that are tender. Discussed treatment options and the patient chooses cryotherapy.  R/B/A of cryotherapy discussed and all questions answered. Verbal consent obtained prior to application of liquid nitrogen via cryogun. 15 seconds x 2 cycles to lesions on the left lateral calf, right medial calf, right lateral thigh, and left medial upper arm. Wound care discussed. Will continue to monitor skin as KAs can continue to form for weeks after discontinuing M7824. If the patient should go back on drug, would consider starting acitretin.

Assessment: 34-year-old female with recurrent metastatic small cell cancer of the cervix with mets to lung/mediastinum, right adrenal. Initially staged at IB and treated with cisplatin/etoposide with a 1.5 year response then found to have metastatic disease to lung s/p VATs, topotecan/paclitaxel/ bevacizumab with response, then progression with mediastinal node causing recurrent laryngeal nerve paralysis treated with carboplatin/gemcitabine, followed by further progression within mediastinum. She then received Ipilimumab/Nivolumab x 4 followed by single agent Nivo for total of 12 doses with initial PET response until PD detected on 3/16/19 PET scan. Enrolled on 15-C-0150, with Topotecan + VX970, C1D1 = 4/10/19, C2D1 = 5/1/19, off treatment on 5/22/19 for PD (increase to left adrenal and left mediastinal mass).   Started week 1 of M7824 treatment 7/17/19.  Nausea refractory to antiemetics since 7/19/2019 associated with constipation. Nausea improved with rotation of antiemetic and  partial relief of constipation.   Bigger issue now per patient is the back/upper leg pain that has gotten worse now radiating through thigh in pattern following L3/L4 dermatome. Not relieved with repositioning as it was  before.   Lab and VS reviewed, patient is OK for Week 3 M7824.   Back leg pain/ sciatica will require further work up to  determine  exact etiology (msk vs tumor related)   ECOG 1
- give IV fluids I L for  mild dehydration
- some relief , but not fully  evacuated.
-  continue   senna colace 2 tabs bid, can   decrease to 2 tabs once daily of  maintenance once regular
- lactulose  20 ml bid until constipation fully relieved.
- hold if stools too loose or if abd cramping too severe
- 40 mg po  potassium chloride in DH
- worse in interim, now radiation down  right  upper leg to knee
- consider sciatic irritation, evaluate for MSK cause vs  tumor involvement
- MRI LS Spine  add on and planned for tonight at 6 PM.
-gabapentin 300 mg start at bedtime with  pan to increase to BID  as needed
- will f/u with  additional  plan for this after scan review  this evening
Consider Palliative care referral for ongoing symptom management.

column2: Agree with assessment and plan. Labs reviewed - appears clinically dehydrated on labs and vitals. NS 1L in day hospital. 40meq repletion. Otherwise nausea/vomiting/constipation improved but still present.    As far as her sciatic-like pain - it started last Thursday but has persisted since onset. It has not worsened overall and she has only a very subtle right leg weakness (4/5 hip flexion, 4/5 knee extension, but otherwise 5/5 and no gait abnormalities). There are no signs of cauda equina on clinical questioning. Of note, a PET in March 2019 showed mild increased update at L3 but there has never been a CT correlate found. She also was on VX970 + topotecan since then and had a mixed response. A CT from May and July does not show any obvious mass or destructive lesions in the lumbar area. When reviewing the CT, there is no obvious mass/obstruction of the spinal canal. No mention of any lumbar spine/paraspinal mets in official reports. She is not known to have any CNS mets – she had a negative brain MRI last week due to intermittent nausea. MRI Lumbar/sacrum today to evaluate. Suspect this is a disc issue but will proceed with caution given her aggressive tumor type.   Okay to proceed with treatment today with M7824.

Assessment: Mr. Cole X is a 63-year-old man with a history of p16-positive SCC of the oropharynx (left tongue base/lingual tonsil) with metastasis to the left neck, initially stage IVA, pT1 (1.9 cm) pN2b (25/43 LNs; 4cm) M0 who has undergone left neck dissection/left base of tongue resection with reconstruction followed by adjuvant weekly cisplatin/radiation and most recently treated on a clinical trial with durvalumab + MEDI0457 (HPV vaccine). column2: Patient seen by me for Dermatology evaluation while in OP12 clinic on 04 Dec 2018. Patient with metastatic HPV+ HNSCC on treatment with M7824 since Aug 2018. Patient has a 4+ week history of a growing keratotic lesion on the right nose - it is mildly tender and non-pruritic. He reports a similar but smaller lesion on the right neck. Patient also reports multiple asymptomatic papules on the face. In addition he reports a 4 week history of a linear rash on his left chest wall - it is asymptomatic, as been stable, and never blistered or crusted.   On exam, the right nasal side wall has a 6mm domed papule with a central keratotic core clinically consistent with a keratoacanthoma. There is a 4mm non-specific keratotic papule on the right neck. Scattered on the bilateral perioral and beard region are multiple 1-2mm white round papules resembling milia. On the bilateral ears (lobes and helices) there are minute keratotic spicules. On the left chest wall is a horizontal linear array of clustered erythematous papules that have a lichenoid appearance, no blisters - the distribution is consistent with either a dermatome or, more likely, a blaschkoid pattern.   The nasal lesion is clinically a keratoacanthoma. This diagnosis was discussed with the patient and his wife. We discussed performing a biopsy of the lesion, freezing the lesion with liquid nitrogen, or monitoring the lesion. He chose to monitor the lesion for now. We discussed the facial papules and their benign appearance. It is likely that this eruption along with the ear spicules are related to the TGFb trap activity of M7824. No treatment initiated as these two skin changes are asymptomatic. The chest eruption is possibly a linear lichen planus-like eruption, possibly associated with the anti-PD-L1 activity of M7824.  A skin biopsy was performed to better characterize the eruption.   Procedure - 4mm skin punch biopsy left chest.  Patient was taken to the OP13 clinic. Risk, benefits, and alternatives of skin biopsy was discussed and the patient singed informed consent. Time out was performed. The area was prepped with an alcohol pad prior to infiltration with lidocaine with epinephrine. A 4mm punch biopsy was performed and the sample was placed in a labeled container of formalin and sent to pathology for processing. A single figure-of-eight 4-0 prolene suture was used to close the wound. Hemostasis was achieved and a dressing was placed. Wound care was discussed. Patient should have suture removed in 10-14 days. patient tolerated the procedure well and left the clinic excellent condition.

Assessment: Mr. X is a 48 yr with HPV16+ metastatic HNSCC to lung and nodes, he is enrolled on protocol 18-c-0056 and is here today for pre-C7 evaluation.   Patient had a new restaging CT scan yesterday which showed  multiple increased pulmonary nodules and right hilar lymphadenopathy with evidence of thrombus within the left atrium concerning for tumor thrombus versus bland thrombus. Interval decrease in other mediastinal lymphadenopathy and pulmonary nodules.   This finding were d/w the patient, his wife and his father.   With regard to treatment activity, it was explained that this mixed response is unusual but can be seen, and considering that the lesions which showed growth at the prior scan are now decreased in size it is possible that this could be a scenario of pseudo-progression other than true progression. And in agreement with the patient and his wife it is considered appropriate at this time to continue with treatment and close restaging.    Considering the evidence of a thrombus in the left atrium, patient was started on 70mg lovenox BID. The CT was unable to discriminate between an actual thrombus and a tumor thrombus. Will d/w the radiology about the need of a new imaging to address this question. Overall management should not change at this time and patient will be continued on anticoagulation.    Blood work are showing a downtrending of the TSH, which is still NOT within normal value. The patient feels well and would like to keep watching the TSH trend rather than increase the synthroid dose.

- Patient is on a ketone diet

column2: Saw Mrs X with MO Fellow Dr Simard and agree with assessment and plan, we will be treating today.  Mrs X was also seen by Dr Brownell, who performed cryoablation of a small new skin lesion on the R cheek, and recommended holding off the phototherapy for the lentiginous lesions of the dorsal hands that Mrs X was considering having.

Called to oncology clinic to evaluate a papule on the cheek. Patient on cycle 3 of M7824 and has a history of chronic sun damage, actinic keratoses, and skin warts. She reports new keratotic papule on the right cheek that is tender but asymptomatic. Patient grew up in Louisiana and got sun burt at the beach she now lives in Florida and gets sun exposure while golfing. On exam the patient is Fitzpatrick skin type 2 with chronic actinic damage with extensive lentiginies. On the right malar cheek there is a 3mm papule with gritty keratotic scale. The patients cheek lesion is clinically an actinic keratosis, but cannot rule out an early keratoacanthoma. Of note, 5 weeks is rather early for KA formation on M7824. Considering the visible location, will treat today with cryotherapy. R/B/A of cryotherapy reviewed with the patient and all questions answered and verbal consent obtained prior to liquid nitrogen application with cryogun. 10 sec thaw time x 2 cycles. wound care discussed. Will continue to monitor for new skin lesions. Should the patient develop keratoacanthomas will consider topical or systemic retinoids.

A non-contrast, low dose CT scan was   performed for attenuation correction and co-registration.  The   patients blood glucose was 99 mg/dl prior to injection.  The study   was performed on a Siemens Biograph 128.      All SUV values given below are in terms of body weight maximums.  SUV   values are taken from Time of Flight images.  For reference purposes,   the SUVavg of liver is approximately 2.5.      Please note that the CT scan performed in conjunction with this study   was used for attenuation correction and co-registration purposes only   using a low dose technique without contrast.      COMPARISON: FDG   Scan Dated:  None available      FINDINGS:      In the visualized areas of the head and neck, FDG uptake appears   physiologic.      In the chest, several right 1 nodules are seen consistent with   metastatic disease. The largest of these is located in the medial   aspect of the superior segment of the right lower lobe  near the   hilum, SUV maximum 15.5, with multiple smaller lesions located   elsewhere in the lower lobe and the periphery of the right middle   lobe. On the left, mild, low-level uptake is seen in the posterior   aspect of the superior segment of the left lower lobe where a small   nodule is seen on CT. CT notes increasing size of known cavitary lung lesion, increasing size of liver lesion, and increasing size of an ill-defined mass in the lower pelvis. The appearance of the lung lesion is consistent with possible pseudoprogression, given that it is a mild increase with new appearance of central necrosis. Similarly the lower pelvic mass appears to be mostly necrotic. However, the liver lesion has not only increased in size but also has a new area that almost appears an additional new lesion in close proximity to the original lesion. This is less convincing for an argument of pseudoprogression and more concerning for progression of disease. We discussed the above findings with the patient and her husband and outlined several paths for future directions:    (1) Continue on M7824 and determine whether the lower pelvis mass, which is likely causing the patient’s increased pain, is amenable for palliative radiation. She would be re-scaned in four weeks to determine whether the above masses continue to grow (progression) or have decreased in size (likely pseudoprogression).   (2) Discontinue M7824 and start standard of care, which would consist of traditional chemotherapy with carboplatin/taxol +/- radiation therapy.   (3) Discontinue M7824 and determine whether she qualifies with any other ongoing clinical trial, particularly with the Phase 1 group at the NIH.   The patient is adamant at this time that she is not interested in further traditional chemotherapy. She had little-to-no clinical benefit with prior chemotherapy but had multiple, intolerable side effects. At this time she is most interested in continuing M7824 while pursuing whether palliative radiation to the lower pelvic mass is an option. At this time she feels that her pain is well controlled with minimal OTC pain medications. We discussed the possibility of obtaining a new biopsy of the liver lesion to send off for tumor genetics that may identify targetable mutations as future treatment options. The patient was evaluated with bone marrow biopsy for cytopenias. Work up diagnostic of low-risk MDS with multilineage dysplasia. Assessment: 63F with metastatic, HPV+ SCC of the rectum with mets to the lung presents to NCI for protocol 18-C-0056, M7824 in HPV-associated malignancies, in ongoing PR.   The patient was evaluated with bone marrow biopsy for cytopenias. Work up diagnostic of low-risk MDS with multilineage dysplasia. NIH Hematology consult recommended supportive care with transfusions, growth factors to maintain ANC > 500, and follow up care with MDS specialist closer to home at either Johns Hopkins Hospital or University of Pennsylvania. Ms. X first started to have lower back and buttock pain in 3/2016. She developed perineal and L buttock numbness. She worked with PT, then saw ortho who treated her with spinal steroid injections, and was sent on to a pain specialist until finally imaging of her pelvis was done and discovered a mass that reportedly wrapped around ""the sacral nerve"".
10/11/16: MRI showed a large rectal mass measuring 4.9x4.8x6.0cm abutting and displacing the cervix and uterus and prominent perirectal and common iliac LNs concerning for metastatic disease.

Sigmoidoscopy observed a 5cm mass covering anterior half of the rectum at 5cm from the anal verge with areas of bleeding and ulceration. The mass was felt to be between rectum and vagina w/ possibility that mass started in posterior vagina or cervix and invaded thru rectal wall.

10/25/16: CT demonstrated centrally necrotic rectal/perirectal mass appearing adherent to the posterior wall of the vagina w/ direct tumor invasion of the posterior upper vaginal wall possible; perirectal adenopathy, as well as adenopathy along the L common iliac chain and possibly along the L para-aortic chain also seen. A colonoscopy was performed.

10/26/2016: The rectal mass bx taken showed at least SCC in situ, with invasive SCC not excluded. The sample was sent for HPV ISH, resulting positive for high risk HPV. Mutation analysis showed no NRAS, BRAF, KRAS mutations detected. A vaginal mass biopsy on 11/15/16 also revealed invasive SCC. She was staged IIIC (T4b N2 M0)

Follow-up MRI Pelvis on 4/5/17 revealed resolution of rectal mass leaving behind an area of rectal wall thickening. Perirectal nodes resolved and L common iliac LN was thought to have responded (though not fully evaluated on scan).

Surveillance CT CAP on 1/30/18 revealed development of metastatic pulmonary nodules. A core biopsy of a R lung nodule on 2/14/18 showed SCC involving lung parenchyma, diffusely and strongly p16 positive. Foundation One identified genomic alterations in  PTEN T319fs*1, ARID1A R727fs*84, EP300 D1399N, KMT2C (MLL3) R4590*, NOTCH1 E1183*, PIK3R1 T645fs*9. MS-Stable.

3/2/18 – 9/21/18: Carboplatin Taxol. She has a mixed response with improvement of lung lesions, but steady progression of a local in-field recurrence involving the cervix, posterior vaginal fornix, and rectum.
CT needle biopsy via transgluteal approach to uterine cervix on 8/17/18 showed fragments of at least high a high grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (SCC in Situ).
MRI Pelvis 10/3/2018 showed 3.6x3.8x2.7cm mass w/in posterior wall of the cervix obscuring the posterior vaginal fornix w/ a contiguous enhancement seen to the adjacent segment of the rectum.
10/22/18 – 11/2/18: Palliative re-XRT (30Gy in twice daily 1.5Gy fx) to pelvic mass + Xeloda
1/23/2019 - Started on trial 18-c-0056 (M7824 in HPV malignancies). Received neupogen support starting on 1/22/19.
- Last seen 2 weeks ago.  At that time, continued to hold M7824 and stopped acitretin.
- Pending JHH Hematology evaluation for MDS this Friday.
- Rash, itch, and Keratoacanthomas resolved off M7824.

Assessment: Karen X is a 63-year-old caucasian female with metastatic, HPV+ SCC of the rectum with mets to the lung presents to NCI for protocol 18-C-0056, M7824 in HPV-associated malignancies, in ongoing PR.   The patient was evaluated with bone marrow biopsy for cytopenias.  Work up diagnostic of MDS with multilineage dysplasia.  Of 20 metaphases, 16 metaphases were normal and 4 metaphases had a 12p deletion. Deletion 12p as a sole abnormality is seen in 3-4% of de novo MDS, and with a generally favorable prognostic association (Bernasconi et al., Brit J Haematol 137:193-205, 2007).  Hematology consult recommends supportive care with transfusions, erythropoietin stimulating agents (ESA), growth factors to maintain ANC > 500, and follow up care with MDS specialist closer to home at either Johns Hopkins Hospital or University of Pennsylvania.  The results were discussed extensively with the patient and she was provided the contact information for referrals.   Recent restaging reviewed with patient showing ongoing partial response (PR).   At this time, we will continue to hold M7824 and wean off retinoid, which may contribute to anemia.  Patient will require transfusions in the Day Hospital for symptomatic anemia. Rashes are improving off treatment.   ECOG 1.
Metastatic HPV+ Rectal SCC with mets to the lung
- Continue to hold Week 37 (Week 33 and 35 were held) of M7824 (bifunctional anti-PD-L1/TGFß Trap fusion protein)
- Transfuse 2 unit PRBC in Day Hospital.  Blood consent on file.
- Status post Hematology consult with bone marrow bx showing MDS-MLD.
- Patient to pursue MDS specialist at UPenn or JHH.
- GCSF to be given if neutropenic.
- ESA to be given if patient remains anemic due to low EPO levels.
- Wean down retinoid to 10 mg/day and then discontinue at next visit in attempt to improve anemia.  Symptoms are improving off of M7824.

column2: Agree with assessment and plan by Dr De Maria. Brielfy Ms X comes to comes to clinic today for Week 37 of treatment with M7824. Her last dose of drug was on 8/20/19. Drug has been held due to fatigue as well as anemia. Since her last visit, she underwent a bone marrow biopsy which showed low risk MDS (see heme note). Given her baseline neutropenia, I suspect MDS was present at baseline. Review of labs today show a grade 3 anemia (hgb 6.7 g/dL; will transfuse 2 units of RBCs today). Scans today show continued PR.   She has been tolerating M7824 q2 weeks well since Jan 2019 (9 months) and only recently became significantly anemic in early Sept. Given that she was started on Acitretin 10mg in mid July for rash/pruritis/KAs and increased to 20mg on 8/7/19, I suspect that her subsequent anemia (onset about 1 month after the dose increase) may in part be due to acitretin. Per review of documented side effects of acitretin, decreased hemoglobina can occur in up to 25% of patients on drug. I suspect that her baseline MDS may have predisposed her to this known side effect of acitretin. Therefore, we will taper her off acitretin at this time. She is currently on 20mg daily and her symptoms are relatively well controlled. At this time, we will decrease her to 10mg daily in order to avoid a flare of her rash/pruritis/KAs. When she returns to clinic in 2 weeks, if her symptoms are still controlled, we will stop the acitretin.  We will continue to hold M7824 at this time as well. Recommended that she get CBC performed next week at home with her primary oncologist and receive RBC is needed.   As far as her MDS, this was likely present at baseline. She will need follow-up with a hematologist for management of this. She has been provided with contacts at JHU and has made an appointment with them in 3 weeks. Also while previously discussed administering ESA given her low epo levels in the setting of MDS, I prefer not to give ESA to this patient given she has another malignancy. Per the boxed warning on the prescribing information for ESA, administration of ESA in cancer patients resulted in shortened overal survival, increased risk of tumor progression in breast, NSCLC, HNSCC, and cervical cancers. Also increased risk of VTEs in this patient population. In addition, since I suspect the acitretin is the cause of her sudden drop in hgb (and not the low grade MDS), we will allow time for RBC recovery with stopping the acitretin in the coming weeks.   RTC 2 weeks for follow-up.

Ms. X first started to have lower back and buttock pain in 3/2016. She developed perineal and L buttock numbness. She worked with PT, then saw ortho who treated her with spinal steroid injections, and was sent on to a pain specialist until finally imaging of her pelvis was done and discovered a mass that reportedly wrapped around ""the sacral nerve"".
10/11/16: MRI showed a large rectal mass measuring 4.9x4.8x6.0cm abutting and displacing the cervix and uterus and prominent perirectal and common iliac LNs concerning for metastatic disease.

Sigmoidoscopy observed a 5cm mass covering anterior half of the rectum at 5cm from the anal verge with areas of bleeding and ulceration. The mass was felt to be between rectum and vagina w/ possibility that mass started in posterior vagina or cervix and invaded thru rectal wall.

10/25/16: CT demonstrated centrally necrotic rectal/perirectal mass appearing adherent to the posterior wall of the vagina w/ direct tumor invasion of the posterior upper vaginal wall possible; perirectal adenopathy, as well as adenopathy along the L common iliac chain and possibly along the L para-aortic chain also seen. A colonoscopy was performed.

10/26/2016: The rectal mass bx taken showed at least SCC in situ, with invasive SCC not excluded. The sample was sent for HPV ISH, resulting positive for high risk HPV. Mutation analysis showed no NRAS, BRAF, KRAS mutations detected. A vaginal mass biopsy on 11/15/16 also revealed invasive SCC. She was staged IIIC (T4b N2 M0)

Follow-up MRI Pelvis on 4/5/17 revealed resolution of rectal mass leaving behind an area of rectal wall thickening. Perirectal nodes resolved and L common iliac LN was thought to have responded (though not fully evaluated on scan).

Surveillance CT CAP on 1/30/18 revealed development of metastatic pulmonary nodules. A core biopsy of a R lung nodule on 2/14/18 showed SCC involving lung parenchyma, diffusely and strongly p16 positive. Foundation One identified genomic alterations in  PTEN T319fs*1, ARID1A R727fs*84, EP300 D1399N, KMT2C (MLL3) R4590*, NOTCH1 E1183*, PIK3R1 T645fs*9. MS-Stable.

3/2/18 – 9/21/18: Carboplatin Taxol. She has a mixed response with improvement of lung lesions, but steady progression of a local in-field recurrence involving the cervix, posterior vaginal fornix, and rectum.
CT needle biopsy via transgluteal approach to uterine cervix on 8/17/18 showed fragments of at least high a high grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (SCC in Situ).
MRI Pelvis 10/3/2018 showed 3.6x3.8x2.7cm mass w/in posterior wall of the cervix obscuring the posterior vaginal fornix w/ a contiguous enhancement seen to the adjacent segment of the rectum.
10/22/18 – 11/2/18: Palliative re-XRT (30Gy in twice daily 1.5Gy fx) to pelvic mass + Xeloda
1/23/2019: Started on trial 18-c-0056 (M7824 in HPV malignancies). Received neupogen support starting on 1/22/19.

column2: Agree with assessment and plan of Dr Shah. Ms X comes to clinic for Week 5 of M7824. Overall she is tolerating treatment relatively well. Hematuria (pink urine) is again noted by the patient. UA confirms the presence of RBCs in the urine. No visible blood clots. Labs including Cr and Hgb stable from last visit. Continues to take pyridium with some relief of urinary spasm. Discussed risk of mucosal bleeding that has been seen with M7824. She denies any gingival bleeding or hemorrhoidal bleeding. We discussed that retrospectively, we have detected some level of mucosal bleeding in approximately 30-40% of patients who have been treated with M7824. The majority of bleeding is clinically insignificant and resolves without intervention. We discussed that should she see blood clots in her urine, significant darkening of her urine, increased hesitancy/signs of urinary retention, she should contact us immediately. After discussing the risk of mucosal bleeding, I discussed that given her low level of hematuria and stable labs, that would could proceed with treatment at this time if she wished to do so. She acknowledged the bleeding risk and would like to proceed as planned. She is aware of the concerning signs of progression and will contact the team if anything worsens. We discussed that the consent form is being amended to include this new side effect and she will be asked to sign it once it is approved. She will be seen by urology tomorrow for formal evaluation however given the low level of hematuria, I am unsure if they will do a cystoscopy. Diarrhea has resolved without recurrence (back to baseline stools). Okay to proceed with treatment.

Due to prior pelvic RT, Ms X has a baseline Grade 3 neutropenia (baseline ANC 0.8 to 1). She received 1 dose of Neupogen prior to enrollment on trial. She has not experienced any episodes of neutropenic fever and has not experienced any prolonged or unresolving infections. Her ANC today is 880 and is at her baseline. While it is a Grade 3, this was present at baseline, is due to her prior RT, and has not been worsened by treatment with M7824. Per review of the protocol, since this ANC is not clinically relevant (chronic, stable, no clinically significant infections), it is okay to proceed with treatment today. Ms X is aware of the risk of neutropenic fever and is familiar with concerning symptoms for which she should seek medical care.

MRI of Pelvis on 10/11/16 showed a large rectal mass measuring 4.9x4.8x6.0cm abutting and displacing the cervix and uterus and prominent perirectal and common iliac LNs concerning for metastatic disease.

Sigmoidoscopy observed a 5cm mass covering anterior half of the rectum at 5cm from the anal verge with areas of bleeding and ulceration. The mass was felt to be between rectum and vagina w/ possibility that mass started in posterior vagina or cervix and invaded thru rectal wall. Further evaluation w/ CT AP on 10/25/16 demonstrated centrally necrotic rectal/perirectal mass appearing adherent to the posterior wall of the vagina w/ direct tumor invasion of the posterior upper vaginal wall possible; perirectal adenopathy, as well as adenopathy along the L common iliac chain and possibly along the L para-aortic chain also seen. A colonoscopy was performed. The rectal mass bx taken on 10/26/16 showed at least SCC in situ, with invasive SCC not excluded. The sample was sent for HPV ISH, resulting positive for high risk HPV. Mutation analysis showed no NRAS, BRAF, KRAS mutations detected. A vaginal mass biopsy on 11/15/16 also revealed invasive SCC. She was staged IIIC (T4b N2 M0)

Follow-up MRI Pelvis on 4/5/17 revealed resolution of rectal mass leaving behind an area of rectal wall thickening. Perirectal nodes resolved and L common iliac LN was thought to have responded (though not fully evaluated on scan).

Surveillance CT CAP on 1/30/18 revealed development of metastatic pulmonary nodules. A core biopsy of a R lung nodule on 2/14/18 showed SCC involving lung parenchyma, diffusely and strongly p16 positive. Foundation One identified genomic alterations in  PTEN T319fs*1, ARID1A R727fs*84, EP300 D1399N, KMT2C (MLL3) R4590*, NOTCH1 E1183*, PIK3R1 T645fs*9. MS-Stable.

3/2/18 – 9/21/18: Carboplatin Taxol. She has a mixed response with improvement of lung lesions, but steady progression of a local in-field recurrence involving the cervix, posterior vaginal fornix, and rectum.
CT needle biopsy via transgluteal approach to uterine cervix on 8/17/18 showed fragments of at least high a high grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (SCC in Situ).
MRI Pelvis 10/3/2018 showed 3.6x3.8x2.7cm mass w/in posterior wall of the cervix obscuring the posterior vaginal fornix w/ a contiguous enhancement seen to the adjacent segment of the rectum.
10/22/18 – 11/2/18: Palliative re-XRT (30Gy in twice daily 1.5Gy fx) to pelvic mass + Xeloda

1. urinary stress incontinence since XRT, starting to improve for which she wears Poise pads

Continues to do spin classes and remains active.

column2: 06/26/11 – Diagnosed with Stage IB-1 endocervical cancer after a routine Pap smear.

08/16/11 – Underwent fertility-sparing surgery and was treated at Mayo Clinic by Dr. Andrea Mariani with robotic assisted bilateral pelvic lymphadenectomy converted to laparotomy due to right external iliac artery injury and repair and complete radical vaginal trachelectomy. Histopathology revealed cerviced with 1.4 cm invasive grade 2/4 endocervical adenocarcinoma embedding to 0.4 cm of the endocervical stroma (1.3 cm total thickness). Negative surgical margins with re-excision of the endocervical margin 3x1.5 cm. No LVI. 0/29 positive pelvic lymph nodes. Did not meet criteria for adjuvant therapy by Sedlis criteria.
12/05/13 – Developed large right pelvic mass. CT C/A/P showed a new 3x3cm splenic hilum lesion, new large (12.5 x 11.7cm) cystic mass in right pelvis. US showed thickened endometrium.

12/18/13 – Underwent ex lap with hysteroscopy and D&C with endometrial curettage, right salpingo-oopherectomy, and right mass removal and splenectomy. Frozen section showed recurrent adenocarcinoma moderately differentiated and final pathology revealed moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma: endometrial curettage recurrent endocervical type and the right ovary showing metastatic endocervical adenocarcinoma. Endometrial polyp showed recurrent endocervical adenocarcinoma and spleen showed epidermoid cyst. Right ovarian tumor positive for p16, negative for WT1, and strongly and diffusely positive for high-risk HPV (family 16) by ISH. The endometrial tumor and right ovarian tumor are similar in appearance to prior endocervical adenocarcinoma.  The decision of leaving the uterus was made for better delivery of pelvic radiation by brachytherapy due to pelvic mass rupture.
12/08/13-5/13/14 – Treated with cisplatin, paclitaxel, and bevacizumab x 6.
06/18/14 - Because of rupture of ovarian mass during surgery the patient referred for external beam RT combined with intracavitary for consolidative radiation.

No evidence of residual malignancy or metastatic disease to the soft tissues or the pelvis. Increased FDG uptake in thyroid gland most likely secondary to underlying thyroiditis.
07/20/14-8/11/14 - Smit sleeve placement for HDR brachytherapy with 4500 cGy to pelvis with boost with 5-6 fractions to upper vagina, endocervix, and endometrium.
11/14/14 - PET/CT showed single focus measuring 9mm and increased uptake in the region of lower uterus which could represent neoplasm (SUV 3.7).

02/13/17 - PET/CT showed new 5mm RUL nodule (non active), 10mm LLL nodule (non-active) since 2015, stable heterogeneity of thyroid gland with increased uptake on the right side (nodule on anterior portion of right lobe).

11/14/17 - Enrolled on 16-C-0154 for treatment with E7 TCR.
12/11/17 - Underwent lymphapheresis as part of protocol.
12/27/17-12/29/17 – Admitted for TCR treatment. Developed subsegmental PE and treated with enoxaparin. Treatment of TCR deferred.
01/16/18-2/5/18 – Admitted for E7 TCR treatment. She received fludarabine and Cytoxan. On 1/25/18, she received E7 TCR T-cells DL3 (1x10^11 cells) followed by IL-2.
02/27/18 - Restaging scans show decrease in both target lesions.
04/18/18 - Restaging scans show increased in LLL target lesion with minimal change in RUL lesion. She also has 2 new FDG-avid lymph nodes.
05/01/18 - C1D1 of 18-C-0056 for treatment with M7824 (anti-PDL1/TGF-beta TRAP) in HPV+ malignancies.
07/11/18 - Developed hematuria. Evaluated by Urology.

07/25/18 - Seen by Urology. Urine culture negative. Urine cytology negative. CT urogram negative for abnormality. TSH uptrended from 33 to 152, and levothyroxine was increased. Restaging scans show slight shrinkage in lesions.

10/16/18 - Week 25 of 18-C-0056. No fatigue, but continues rash on cheeks and intermittent hematuria. Stable H/H. CT scan shows stable disease

column2: Called to day hospital to evaluate pruritic eruption in patient taking M7824 since 5/28/19. Patient reports papules appearing on her distal legs, left forearm, and possibly face. She is not clear as to how long they have been present, but she does note that the eruption has gotten worse over time. She does not endorse pruritus, however most of the small papules on the legs are excoriated with a central heme crust. The 2-3mm flesh colored papules on the left forearm clustered near the elbow are not excoriated. No lesions are suggestive of keratoacanthoma today, however the excoriated lesions are difficult to assess. The patient has a non-specific papular eruption that she scratches. The small papules appear to have minimal inflammation and no scale. Arthropod assault, contact dermatitis, and other sub-acute forms of dermatitis are within the differential. An eczematous irAE from the M7824 is also possible. For now, agree with symptomatic management with antihistamines and topical HC 2.5%. Consider going to more potent topical steroids if eruption and pruritus progresses. Will monitor for keratoacanthomas.
